   106	    /// [`crate::parse::FrameworkScriptProgram::Shared`] for other carriers).
   107	    /// `false` means the raw source passed through unchanged (non-carrier
   108	    /// files, or a carrier with no extractable script), where the eval program
   109	    /// covers different bytes than a script-program walk would.
   110	    ///
   111	    /// Carrier-NEUTRAL: a non-Vue carrier blanks from the producer's recorded
   112	    /// `script_regions` (both instance + module blocks), Vue keeps its exact
   113	    /// `extract_vue_script_content` behaviour, and a non-carrier passes through.
   114	    ///
   115	    /// Extraction is gated on the file's LANGUAGE CLASSIFICATION, never on the
   116	    /// raw text: `canonical_id` classifies through the single static registry
   117	    /// (the same authority `resolve_route_type_edge` uses), and ONLY a
   118	    /// framework-carrier file may script-extract when no parse artifact is
   119	    /// available. A non-carrier `.ts` / `.d.ts` whose TEXT happens to contain a
   120	    /// `<script ...>` ... `</script>` pair — a JSDoc `@example` block in a
   121	    /// package declaration file (vue-router@5, @regle/core, unhead dist all
   122	    /// ship one) — passes through UNCHANGED; the former unconditional forgiving
   123	    /// raw scan blanked such a file down to its documentation example,
   124	    /// destroying its whole type surface (empty shallow inventory → every
   125	    /// dependent member value unresolvable).
   126	    pub(crate) fn build_eval_script_source_with_extraction(
   127	        canonical_id: &str,
   128	        source: &str,
   129	        framework_parse: Option<&verter_compiler::framework_common::FrameworkParseArtifact>,
   130	    ) -> (String, bool) {
   131	        // A NON-Vue framework carrier blanks NEUTRALLY from the producer's
   132	        // recorded `script_regions` (BOTH the instance and module script blocks)
   133	        // — so a `.svelte` eval-source carries both scripts at their raw carrier
   134	        // offsets with the markup/styles whitespace-blanked. A new carrier needs
   135	        // no per-adapter branch here. The blanked text IS a position-preserving
   136	        // extracted script (the eval program over it is shareable), so the
   137	        // provenance is `true`.
   138	        if let Some(artifact) = framework_parse {
   139	            let is_vue = crate::typeinfo::adapters::vue::vue_parse(artifact).is_some();
   140	            if !is_vue {
   141	                let mut spans: Vec<(u32, u32)> = artifact
   142	                    .common()
   143	                    .script_regions()
   144	                    .iter()
   145	                    .map(|region| (region.span.start, region.span.end))
   146	                    .filter(|(start, end)| end > start)
   147	                    .collect();
   148	                spans.sort_by_key(|(start, _)| *start);
   149	                // Even with NO script regions (a pure-markup `.svelte`) the
   150	                // eval-source is the FULLY-BLANKED, line-preserving source — never
   151	                // the raw markup. `build_position_preserving_script_source` over an
   152	                // empty span set blanks every non-line-terminator byte, so a shared
   153	                // eval-source consumer parses an empty TS program, not HTML.
   154	                let blanked =
   155	                    crate::host_resolve::build_position_preserving_script_source(source, &spans);
   156	                return (blanked, true);
   157	            }
   158	        }
   159	        // Vue extraction consumes parser-owned spans only. A classified
   160	        // carrier without its registered artifact fails closed by preserving
   161	        // offsets while exposing no markup or script bytes to type evaluation.
   162	        let parsed = framework_parse.and_then(crate::typeinfo::adapters::vue::vue_parse);
   163	        // A file with NO parse artifact script-extracts ONLY when its
   164	        // canonical CLASSIFIES as a framework carrier. A non-carrier file's
   165	        // raw source is already script: `<script>` text inside it is
   166	        // documentation/data, not structure, and the forgiving raw scan must
   167	        // never blank it (typed classification decides, never text sniffing).
   168	        if parsed.is_none()
   169	            && !verter_language::LanguageRegistry::global()
   170	                .classify_static(canonical_id)
   171	                .static_resolution()
   172	                .is_framework_carrier()
   173	        {
   174	            return (source.to_string(), false);
   175	        }
   400	/// `ctx` is the producer-emitted anchor context (producing canonical +
   401	/// contributor index) the minted authored locators / span origins anchor to.
   402	pub fn lower_top_level_statement(
   403	    stmt: &Statement<'_>,
   404	    ctx: StatementLowerCtx<'_>,
   405	    source: &str,
   406	    env: &mut EvalEnv,
   407	) {
   408	    let parts = lower_statement_parts(stmt, source);
   409	    register_statement_parts(parts, ctx, env);
   410	}
   411	
   412	/// Lower ONE top-level statement to its TRANSIENT declaration parts, without
   413	/// registering anything. The single dispatch both the production registration
   414	/// walk and the in-crate lowering tests consume — one lowering path, no fork.
   415	pub fn lower_statement_parts(stmt: &Statement<'_>, source: &str) -> LoweredStatementParts {
   416	    let mut out = LoweredStatementParts::default();
   417	    collect_statement_parts(stmt, source, &mut out);
   418	    out
   419	}
   420	
   421	/// Lower one top-level statement under Svelte 5 runes semantics.
   422	///
   423	/// This is deliberately a narrow extension of [`lower_statement_parts`], not a
   424	/// second declaration-lowering engine: the ordinary statement walk produces
   425	/// the complete transient declaration inventory first, then this function
   426	/// replaces only an inferred top-level variable annotation whose initializer
   427	/// is a supported identity-like rune call (`$state`, `$state.raw`,
   428	/// `$state.snapshot`, `$state.eager`, `$derived`, or `$derived.by`). Explicit
   429	/// TypeScript/JSDoc annotations continue to win, and callers must select this
   430	/// entry only after the component's scope-aware mode classifier has proved
   431	/// runes mode. Consequently a legacy store accessor named `$state` is never
   432	/// reinterpreted as a rune.
   433	pub fn lower_svelte_runes_statement_parts(
   434	    stmt: &Statement<'_>,
   435	    source: &str,
   436	) -> LoweredStatementParts {
   437	    let mut out = lower_statement_parts(stmt, source);
   438	    apply_svelte_rune_initializer_inference(stmt, source, &mut out.value_decls);
   439	    out
   440	}
   441	
   442	/// Mint the stored facts/locators from TRANSIENT statement parts and register
   443	/// them on `env`, discarding the transient typed IR.
   444	///
   445	/// Public alongside [`lower_statement_parts`] so a demand-time producer can
   446	/// SPLIT the two steps — retain the transient lowered bodies it needs for
   447	/// fact-production (the decl-body content fingerprint) between lowering and
   448	/// registration — without forking the lowering path. The retained transients
   449	/// remain fact-production intermediates; only the minted facts/locators are
   450	/// registered.
   451	pub fn register_statement_parts(
   452	    parts: LoweredStatementParts,
   453	    ctx: StatementLowerCtx<'_>,
   454	    env: &mut EvalEnv,
   455	) {
   456	    let LoweredStatementParts {
   457	        type_decls,
   458	        value_decls,
   459	        aug_type_decls,
   460	        aug_value_decls,
   461	        alias_default_type_to,
   462	    } = parts;
   463	    for parts in type_decls {
   464	        env.add_type(mint_type_decl(
   465	            &parts,
   466	            &ctx.build.canonical_id,
   467	            ctx.statement_owner.owner,
   468	        ));
   469	    }
   470	    for parts in value_decls {
   471	        env.add_value(mint_value_decl(&parts, &ctx.build.canonical_id, ctx));
   472	    }
   473	    for (scope, parts) in aug_type_decls {
   474	        env.add_augmentation_type(
   475	            scope,
   476	            mint_type_decl(&parts, &ctx.build.canonical_id, ctx.statement_owner.owner),
   477	        );
   478	    }
   479	    for (scope, parts) in aug_value_decls {
   480	        env.add_augmentation_value(scope, mint_value_decl(&parts, &ctx.build.canonical_id, ctx));
   481	    }
   482	    if let Some(name) = alias_default_type_to {
   483	        alias_default_export_type_symbol(env, ctx.statement_owner.owner, &name);
   484	    }
   485	}
   486	
   487	fn collect_statement_parts(stmt: &Statement<'_>, source: &str, out: &mut LoweredStatementParts) {
   488	    match stmt {
   489	        Statement::TSTypeAliasDeclaration(decl) => {
   490	            out.type_decls.push(lower_named_type_alias_parts(
   491	                decl,
   492	                source,
   493	                decl.id.name.to_string(),
   494	            ));
   495	        }
   496	        Statement::TSInterfaceDeclaration(decl) => {
   497	            out.type_decls.push(lower_named_interface_parts(
   498	                decl,
   499	                source,
   500	                decl.id.name.to_string(),
   501	            ));
   502	        }
   503	        Statement::TSModuleDeclaration(module) => {
   504	            collect_module_declaration(module, source, out, None);
   505	        }
   506	        Statement::TSGlobalDeclaration(global) => {
   507	            collect_augmentation_block(&global.body, source, out, AugmentationScopeKind::Global);
   508	        }
   509	        Statement::ClassDeclaration(decl) => {
   510	            collect_class(decl, source, out);
   511	        }
   512	        Statement::TSEnumDeclaration(decl) => {
   513	            collect_enum(decl, out);
   514	        }
   515	        Statement::FunctionDeclaration(func) => {
   516	            if let Some(parts) = lower_function_parts(func, source) {
   517	                out.value_decls.push(parts);
   518	            }
   519	        }
   520	        Statement::VariableDeclaration(var_decl) => {
   521	            for decl in &var_decl.declarations {
   522	                if let Some(parts) = lower_variable_parts(decl, var_decl.kind, source, None) {
   523	                    out.value_decls.push(parts);
   524	                }
   525	            }
   526	        }
   527	        Statement::ExportNamedDeclaration(export) => {
   528	            if let Some(ref decl) = export.declaration {
   529	                collect_from_declaration(decl, source, out);
   530	            }
   531	        }
   532	        Statement::ExportDefaultDeclaration(export) => match &export.declaration {
   533	            ExportDefaultDeclarationKind::FunctionDeclaration(func) => {
   534	                if let Some(parts) = lower_function_parts(func, source) {
   535	                    out.value_decls.push(parts);
  1180	            .type_header_in(owner, name)
  1181	            .is_some()
  1182	    }

  1184	    /// Whether `name` is a file-scope VALUE symbol (header-level,
  1185	    /// including synthesised symbols).
  1186	    pub fn has_value_symbol(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
  1187	        self.decl_bodies.header_index().value_header(name).is_some()
  1188	            || self.synthesised_export_decl_key(name).is_some()
  1189	    }
  1190	
  1191	    pub(crate) fn has_value_symbol_in(&self, owner: TopLevelOwnerId, name: &str) -> bool {
  1192	        self.decl_bodies
  1193	            .header_index()
  1194	            .value_header_in(owner, name)
  1195	            .is_some()
  1196	            || self
  1197	                .synthesised_value_symbols
  1198	                .contains_key(&DeclBindingKey::new(owner, name))
  1199	    }

  1201	    /// Canonical one-way lexical parent for a carrier instance owner.
  1202	    ///
  1203	    /// The relation is derived exclusively from the validated owner table. An
  1204	    /// instance sees a sole module owner; module/frontmatter owners have no
  1205	    /// parent, and multiple module owners are ambiguous and fail closed.
  1206	    pub(crate) fn validated_lexical_parent_owner(
  1207	        &self,
  1208	        owner: TopLevelOwnerId,
  1209	    ) -> Option<TopLevelOwnerId> {
  1210	        self.decl_bodies
  1211	            .owner_table()
  1212	            .validated_lexical_parent_owner(owner)
  1213	    }
  1214	
  1215	    fn lexical_owner_chain(&self, owner: TopLevelOwnerId) -> impl Iterator<Item = TopLevelOwnerId> {
  1216	        std::iter::once(owner).chain(self.validated_lexical_parent_owner(owner))
  1217	    }
  1218	
  1219	    pub(crate) fn visible_value_binding(
  1220	        &self,
  1221	        owner: TopLevelOwnerId,
  1222	        name: &str,
  1223	    ) -> Option<LexicalValueBinding<'_>> {
  1224	        for candidate in self.lexical_owner_chain(owner) {
  1225	            if let Some(target) = self
  1226	                .owner_import_targets
  1227	                .get(&DeclBindingKey::new(candidate, name))
  1228	            {
  1229	                return Some(LexicalValueBinding::Import(target));
  1230	            }

  1232	                return Some(LexicalValueBinding::Local(candidate));
  1233	            }

  1236	    }

  1572	    ) -> DemandLower {

  1574	        // body-less miss — NOT a lease-pin break.

  1577	        };

   677	fn prepare_local_value_decl_outcome_with_base(
   678	    canonical_id: &Arc<str>,
   679	    state: &ShallowFileState,
   680	    owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   681	    symbol_name: &str,
   682	    dep_edges: Option<&FxHashMap<String, String>>,
   683	    import_canonicalization: &ImportCanonicalization,
   684	    shared_name_resolution_base: Option<&SharedNameResolutionBase>,
   685	    interner: &IdentityInterner,
   686	) -> PreparedDeclOutcome<PreparedValueDecl> {
   687	    let lowered: Arc<LoweredValueDecl> = match state.value_decl_outcome_in(owner, symbol_name) {
   688	        DemandOutcome::LeaseMiss => return PreparedDeclOutcome::LeaseMiss,
   689	        DemandOutcome::Ready(None) => return PreparedDeclOutcome::Ready(None),
   690	        DemandOutcome::Ready(Some(lowered)) => lowered,
   691	    };
   692	    if state.is_import_local_in(owner, symbol_name) {
   693	        return PreparedDeclOutcome::Ready(None);
   694	    }
   695	
   696	    let mut prepared = PreparedValueDecl::new(
   697	        ResolvedRootIdentity::new_in_owner(
   698	            Arc::clone(canonical_id),
   699	            owner,
   700	            interner.intern(symbol_name),
   701	        ),
   702	        lowered.kind,
   703	    );
   704	    prepared.type_annotation = lowered.type_annotation.clone();
   705	    prepared.signatures = lowered.signatures.clone();
   706	    prepared.object_shape = lowered.object_shape.clone();
   707	    prepared.enum_members = lowered.enum_members.clone();
   708	
   709	    let authored_route = match &prepared.type_annotation.reference_head {
   710	        verter_type_expr::facts::AuthoredReferenceHeadFact::Bare { local_name, .. } => {
   711	            Some((Arc::clone(local_name), Arc::<[Arc<str>]>::from([])))
   712	        }
   713	        verter_type_expr::facts::AuthoredReferenceHeadFact::Qualified {
   714	            local_root,
   715	            member_path,
   716	            ..
   717	        } => Some((Arc::clone(local_root), Arc::clone(member_path))),
   718	        _ => None,
   719	    };
   720	    if let Some((local_name, member_path)) = authored_route {
   721	        if let Some(target) =
   722	            state
   723	                .owner_import_targets
   724	                .get(&verter_type_expr::DeclBindingKey::new(
   725	                    owner,
   726	                    local_name.as_ref(),
   727	                ))
   728	        {
   729	            if target.is_namespace {
   730	                // A namespace binding is not itself a declaration identity, and
   731	                // preparation resolves nothing — so an unroutable first hop is
   732	                // SKIPPED, never a preparation failure. This mirrors the policy
   733	                // `insert_value_space_import_resolutions` states explicitly: an
   734	                // unrelated non-canonicalizable binding must not make every
   735	                // local value declaration in the owner unavailable. Failing here
   736	                // would degrade `typeof variant` — and hover/definition on that
   737	                // binding — from "unresolved `Ref`" to nothing at all.
   738	                //
   739	                // The shared namespace-member resolver validates and
   740	                // canonicalizes the selected export at demand time. Preparation
   741	                // retains only the authored first-hop edge, with the
   742	                // FILE-DEFAULT top-level owner every sibling arm records for an
   743	                // ordinary declaring file — `owner` participates in the derived
   744	                // `Hash`/serde identity, so the SFC-instance owner would be a
   745	                // stable-but-wrong discriminant.
   746	                let routed = member_path.split_first().and_then(|(member, rest)| {
   747	                    let target_canonical = dep_edges
   748	                        .and_then(|edges| edges.get(&target.source_specifier))
   749	                        .cloned()
   750	                        .unwrap_or_default();
   751	                    (!target_canonical.is_empty()).then(|| PreparedExternalDep {
   752	                        local_name: local_name.to_string(),
   753	                        source_specifier: target.source_specifier.clone(),
   754	                        imported_name: member.to_string(),
   755	                        member_path: Arc::from(rest),
   756	                        canonical_id: target_canonical,
   757	                        owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId::ordinary_file(),
   758	                        symbol_name: member.to_string(),
   759	                    })
   760	                });
   761	                if let Some(edge) = routed {
   762	                    push_unique_external_dep(&mut prepared.external_deps, edge);
   763	                }
   764	            } else {
   765	                let Some(identity) = import_canonicalization.final_resolution.get(
   766	                    &verter_type_expr::DeclBindingKey::new(owner, local_name.as_ref()),
   767	                ) else {
   768	                    return PreparedDeclOutcome::Failed(PreparationFailure::MissingExternalOwner {
   769	                        local_name: local_name.to_string(),
   770	                    });
   771	                };
   772	                push_unique_external_dep(
   773	                    &mut prepared.external_deps,
   774	                    PreparedExternalDep {
   775	                        local_name: local_name.to_string(),
   776	                        source_specifier: target.source_specifier.clone(),
   777	                        imported_name: target.imported_name.clone(),
   778	                        member_path,
   779	                        canonical_id: identity.canonical_id.to_string(),
   780	                        owner: identity.owner,
   781	                        symbol_name: identity.symbol_name.to_string(),
   782	                    },
   783	                );
   784	            }
   785	        }
   786	    }
   787	
   788	    // name_resolution for type annotations / `typeof` references that
   789	    // reference imported or local symbols in the defining file — the per-FILE
   790	    // value-space base table (file symbols, then imports; a re-export-hop
   791	    // import canonicalizes to the FINAL defining file through the barrel-final
   792	    // canonicalization, same authority as the type rail; otherwise the barrel
   793	    // fallback applies), shared across every value decl of the file. Keys and
   794	    // identities are interned `Arc<str>` allocations minted through the
   795	    // store-owned pool.
   796	    prepared.name_resolution = match shared_name_resolution_base {
   797	        Some(base) => Arc::clone(base),
   798	        None => match build_value_name_resolution_base(
   799	            canonical_id,
   800	            state,
   801	            owner,
   802	            dep_edges,
   803	            import_canonicalization,
   804	            interner,
   805	        ) {
   806	            Ok(base) => Arc::new(base),
   807	            Err(failure) => return PreparedDeclOutcome::Failed(failure),
   808	        },
   809	    };
   810	
   811	    let hash_u64 = u64::from_le_bytes(state.whole_hash[..8].try_into().unwrap_or_default());
   812	    prepared.cache_deps.defining_file = Some((canonical_id.as_ref().to_string(), hash_u64));
   813	
   814	    PreparedDeclOutcome::Ready(Some(prepared))
   815	}

   817	/// Prepare a named exported value declaration after routing has selected the
   818	/// defining file.
   819	pub fn prepare_exported_value_decl(
   820	    canonical_id: &str,
   821	    state: &ShallowFileState,

   440	/// Lease-aware augmentation preparation. A broken-lease augmenter body
   441	/// surfaces the DISTINCT `LeaseMiss` so cross-file stitching cannot warm-admit
   442	/// an under-merged surface.
   443	pub(crate) fn prepare_augmentation_type_decl_outcome_in(
   444	    canonical_id: &Arc<str>,
   445	    state: &ShallowFileState,
   446	    scope: &verter_semantic::analysis::type_eval::AugmentationScopeKind,
   447	    owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   448	    symbol_name: &str,
   449	    dep_edges: Option<&FxHashMap<String, String>>,
   450	    import_canonicalization: &ImportCanonicalization,
   451	    interner: &IdentityInterner,
   452	) -> PreparedDeclOutcome<PreparedTypeDecl> {
   453	    let lowered = match state.augmentation_type_decl_outcome_in(scope, owner, symbol_name) {
   454	        DemandOutcome::LeaseMiss => return PreparedDeclOutcome::LeaseMiss,
   455	        DemandOutcome::Ready(None) => return PreparedDeclOutcome::Ready(None),
   456	        DemandOutcome::Ready(Some(lowered)) => lowered,
   457	    };
   458	    // Augmentation bodies share the containing file's exact import namespace.
   459	    // The canonicalization must therefore be the one built with the containing
   460	    // prepared bundle under the active StoreView; an empty/default map would
   461	    // discard an imported base symbol's authoritative target owner. The
   462	    // body's dependency edges classify through the SAME shared core as
   463	    // file-scope declarations, so a referenced import without an
   464	    // owner-exact canonicalization entry fails preparation with
   465	    // `MissingExternalOwner` instead of silently preparing Complete.
   466	    //
   467	    // The AUGMENTED BASE is itself an implicit dependency: when the
   468	    // containing file IMPORTS the augmented name, the contributor stitches
   469	    // onto that imported base, so preparation requires the canonicalization
   470	    // to carry the base's OWNER-EXACT `(owner, name)` entry — an entry
   471	    // recorded under a different lexical owner never satisfies it.
   472	    if state.is_import_local_in(owner, symbol_name)
   473	        && !import_canonicalization
   474	            .final_resolution
   475	            .contains_key(&verter_type_expr::DeclBindingKey::new(owner, symbol_name))
   476	    {
   477	        return PreparedDeclOutcome::Failed(PreparationFailure::MissingExternalOwner {
   478	            local_name: symbol_name.to_string(),
   479	        });
   480	    }
   481	    let deps = state.classify_lowered_type_deps(owner, symbol_name, lowered.as_ref());
   482	    match prepare_type_decl_from_lowered(
   483	        canonical_id,
   484	        state,
   485	        owner,
   486	        symbol_name,
   487	        lowered.as_ref(),
   488	        Some(deps.as_ref()),
   489	        dep_edges,
   490	        Some(scope),
   491	        import_canonicalization,
   492	        None,
   493	        interner,
   494	    ) {
   495	        Ok(prepared) => PreparedDeclOutcome::Ready(Some(prepared)),
   496	        Err(failure) => PreparedDeclOutcome::Failed(failure),
   497	    }
   498	}

   500	/// Assemble the common prepared-declaration shell from producer-owned facts.
   501	/// Both strict cache preparation and the projection-only authored-partial
   502	/// path route here, so binder, member-index, heritage, and invalidation facts
   503	/// cannot drift between the two representations.
   504	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   505	fn finish_prepared_type_decl(
   506	    canonical_id: &Arc<str>,
   507	    state: &ShallowFileState,
   508	    owner: verter_type_expr::TopLevelOwnerId,
   509	    symbol_name: &str,
   510	    lowered: &LoweredTypeDecl,
   511	    deps: &ClassifiedTypeDeps,
   512	    external_deps: Vec<PreparedExternalDep>,
   513	    name_resolution: SharedNameResolutionBase,
   514	    interner: &IdentityInterner,
   515	) -> Result<PreparedTypeDecl, PreparationFailure> {
   516	    let mut prepared = PreparedTypeDecl::new(
   517	        ResolvedRootIdentity::new_in_owner(
   518	            Arc::clone(canonical_id),
   519	            owner,
   520	            interner.intern(symbol_name),
   521	        ),
   522	        lowered.kind,
   523	    );
   524	    // A merged interface carries its ordered contributor SLOTS so body
   525	    // lowering interns a `MergedDecl` peer-merge carrier rather than
   526	    // collapsing to a bare intersection.
   527	    if lowered.body.is_merged() {
   528	        prepared
   529	            .set_merged_contributors(lowered.body.contributors().len())
   530	            .map_err(|overflow| PreparationFailure::AuthoredOrdinalOverflow {
   531	                count: overflow.count,
   532	            })?;
   533	    }
   534	    prepared.type_parameters = lowered.narrow_type_parameters.clone();
   535	    prepared.vue_ignored_heritage = Arc::clone(&lowered.vue_ignored_heritage);
   536	    prepared.local_deps = deps.local_deps.clone();
   537	    prepared.external_deps = external_deps;
   538	    prepared.name_resolution = name_resolution;
   539	
   540	    // Populate cache deps for invalidation
   541	    let hash_u64 = u64::from_le_bytes(state.whole_hash[..8].try_into().unwrap_or_default());
   542	    prepared.cache_deps.defining_file = Some((canonical_id.as_ref().to_string(), hash_u64));
   543	    prepared.cache_deps.local_closure_participants = deps.local_deps.clone();
   544	
   545	    // The classification FACTS (member index / wrapper shape / projection
   546	    // class) were produced ONCE at lazy decl-body lowering time from the
   547	    // transient contributor bodies (the shared `verter_semantic` classifiers
   548	    // over the same lowering that minted the fingerprint) and stored on the
   549	    // memo record — the prepared surface COPIES them. No re-classification,
   550	    // no locator deref, no dispatch, no eager `Instantiate` at prepare time.
   551	    prepared.member_index = lowered.member_index.clone();
   552	    prepared.wrapper_shape = lowered.wrapper_shape.clone();
   553	    prepared.projection_class = lowered.projection_class.clone();
   554	    prepared.heritage_bases = Arc::clone(&lowered.heritage_bases);
   555	    prepared.key_domain_closedness = lowered.key_domain_closedness.clone();
   556	    Ok(prepared)
   557	}

   559	/// Prepare a named exported type declaration after routing has selected the
   560	/// defining file.
   561	pub fn prepare_exported_type_decl(
   562	    canonical_id: &str,
   563	    state: &ShallowFileState,
   564	    exported_name: &str,
   565	    dep_edges: Option<&FxHashMap<String, String>>,
   566	    interner: &IdentityInterner,

   574	    // canonicalization (that is threaded by the host-materialised caches); a
   575	    // re-export hop falls back to the barrel here. Production resolution goes
   576	    // through the caches, which thread the real canonicalization.
   577	    let Some(mut prepared) = prepare_local_type_decl_in(

   585	    )?
   586	    else {

   588	    };

   590	    prepared.provenance.route_kind = Some("direct".to_string());
   591	    Ok(Some(prepared))
   592	}

   429	/// Map each DIRECT sibling member of a namespaced declaration's enclosing

   441	/// - File-scope decl (`origin = None`): file-scope `namespace NS { ... }` TYPE

   444	///   prepared-type cache, a value sibling through `prepare_local_value_decl`.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:150:| C1-AC-5 | `AttemptOutcome::{Complete, NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal}` covers **every** non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt — full coverage, not one load point | Discharged structurally, not by sampling. Per C1-AC-7 and the Authority/fallback order clause, the observation interface is the *only* surface an I/O-free (C2-shaped) caller can reach a non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation through — `ResolverContext` itself can call `ensure_loaded`/`wait_or_drive`, so it is not usable I/O-free. "Every reachable operation" therefore reduces to "every method on this one finite, closed trait." The trait is defined so every method returns `AttemptOutcome<T>` at the type level (never a bare `T`, `Result<T, _>`, or a call that can block) — a non-conforming method is a compile error at authoring time, not a gap a test could miss. Gate: one exhaustive test double (`impl <ObservationInterface> for TestDouble`) that must implement every trait method to compile; a method added later that does not return `AttemptOutcome<T>` fails to compile at the double, not at a sampled runtime assertion. If a future operation cannot be expressed this way, that is itself a Fork-4-reopening discovery (see Abort/rescope), not a reason to fall back to sampling. |

Whole-workspace closure-based dependency-firewall test with A5-DD1 equality-pinned exception (target-condition-precise, C1 removal gate). Deleted verter_audit_no_upward_deps + no_session_dep.rs; kept audit_substrate_isolation as named grandfathered guard (explicit decision). Landed as true linear fast-forward: accepted_tree == candidate_tree, no landing_equivalence artifact needed. Reviewed candidate preserved from GC via tag program-history/B1-reviewed-candidate. Prerequisite: feat(gate) memory-ceiling tooling landed separately at 5c24d22a5 (not a ledger block) after this machine's 2nd OOM incident this program; real capped canonical gate run (--build-jobs 2 --test-threads 2 --memory-limit 8GiB) terminal VERDICT with exactly 2 pre-existing load-sensitive flakes independently proven non-causal via isolated reruns on both baseline and candidate trees; one bounded fix cycle (stale discrimination-proof regenerated, mislabeled evidence file corrected), reattested PASS. Non-blocking discovery, routed not resolved: plausible (unconfirmed) RSS-driver lead in verter_session SURFACE 2 OnceLock-memoized syn-AST scans (architecture_guards.rs, output_projector_residual_guards.rs) — recommended as its own investigation thread."
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round1-reopen-scoping-ruling.md:5722:   276	notes = "Gap-analysis-only block: every one of BF1's 7 numbered exit criteria and all owned-scope bullets independently verified already satisfied by the previously-landed, maintainer-ratified AMD-005 package. REOPEN #1 (legitimate, new finding not previously reviewed): the parallelism consult found exit criterion #6 (BF2 performance cells frozen before BF2 work begins) was unmet — performance-gates.toml had no BF2 cells. Resolved by measuring the already-authored, BF1-owned official-case enumeration tool (generate-official-case-manifests.mjs) against the pinned oracle sources — a legitimate before-BF2-exists reference measurement, not criterion-selection-after-candidate-measurement — freezing BF2_VUE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE/BF2_SVELTE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE (10-invocation session, wall/RSS bounds, SHA-256 output-oracle, exact-equality work counters, operationally-proven zero-network via a live curl-denial control). First review pass: architecture BLOCKING (cells mislabeled as covering golden/compiler-invocation generation, which was never measured); fixed by rescoping the operation text to enumeration/classification only and adding an explicit open/deferred row in performance-impact.md for the heavier compiler-invocation+golden workload (matching the existing BV1/BS1/B6/C4 deferred-row pattern). Reattested PASS, no threshold values changed, no scope creep. candidate_sha == accepted_sha exactly (no landing squash needed beyond the one already-squashed commit). Prior review record: architecture PASS (DAG sequencing B1->BF1->BF2->BF3->{B2,B3} confirmed coherent, zero production diff, emitter-mapping dispositions spot-checked), adversarial found one BLOCKING governance finding (AMD-005 §15.1's ratification quotation cited the wrong reviewed-package SHA — pre-fix ce1d0e4688 instead of PASS-reattested 7442bb9060; citation-only, substance always correct) — escalated per STOP conditions, architecture-authorized as non-discretionary record repair (no new maintainer ratification required, governance §10), landed as standalone commit f1b59d2dd. AMD-005 (Framework Compiler Conformance Rescope) itself maintainer-ratified and landed at 34fe8167f (housekeeping squash of the original four-commit landing sequence — content byte-identical, tree unchanged; superseded pre-fix candidate ce1d0e4688/1ff1f83d8e, reviewed package 7442bb9060/69502487b, ratified bundle aa757eecc/0c078357b, original ratification-record commit ade8a301b, preserved on branch backup/pre-amd005-squash).    205	**Exit:** project-aware compilation cannot accept another semantic engine or stale/mismatched facts.
   206	
   207	## C3 — Closed Vue runtime macro projection
   208	
   209	**Predecessors:** `C2`.
   210	
   211	Batch exact demands, deduplicate shared roots, stop at broad constructor terminals, follow imports/generics/unions/mapped/indexed forms only until the closed answer, and return typed degradation/dependencies/profile.
   212	
   213	**Exit:** codegen receives only facts it consumes.
   214	
   215	## C4 — Zero-work, batch-shape, and regime-equivalence proof
   216	
   217	**Predecessors:** `B5`, `C3`.
   218	
   219	Prove no-demand zero initialization, Svelte zero Vue/native projection, aggregate-project-once batch shape, and equal direct/prepared/managed semantics.
   220	
   221	**Exit:** optional semantics are physically absent when not requested.

     1	# C1 — Converge `ModuleResolverCore` and non-flow `TypeInfoCore`
     2	
     3	**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** Foundational
     4	(`program-dag.toml:162`). **Predecessors:** `A6`, `B1`, `B2` (`program-dag.toml:163`) — all three
     5	`ACCEPTED` (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:216,237,447`).
     6	
     7	**Rulings applied.** This charter was rewritten to conform to `ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md` (the
     8	architecture challenge against the prior draft's four open forks). All four of that draft's proposed
     9	positions were **REJECTED**. See "Rulings applied" below for the four verdicts and their consequences; do
    10	not relitigate them here.
    11	
    12	## Context — why this is bigger than program.md's five lines
    13	
    14	`program.md:191-197` gives C1 five lines: converge two logical owners, preserve resolution semantics,
    15	use immutable observation views, return batched `NeedInputs`, exclude flow. Read literally that sounds
    16	like an in-place refactor. **It is not.** The four rulings resolve every genuine fork in the direction
    17	that costs the most, and the charter says so plainly rather than understating it:
    18	
    19	1. **This is a real crate extraction, now, not a deferred one.** `resolver_core` (`pub mod`, 59 files —
    20	   including `component_meta/` (6 files) and `component_meta_query_engine/` (14 files): verified, neither
    21	   holds a `&VerterHost`/`Arc<VerterHost>` field or parameter in production code, only doc-comment mentions
    22	   and `#[cfg(test)]` `VerterHost::new` fixture construction identical to the pattern already accepted for
    23	   `resolver_core`'s own top-level `*_tests.rs` files, so both subdirectories move with the rest of the
    24	   wildcard, not a carve-out — see the convergence map below),
    25	   the private `resolver_store` module, and the `pub(crate)` `project_semantic_dispatch` module —
    26	   all three currently living inside `verter_session` (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:332,341-344`)
    27	   — physically relocate into the existing `verter_semantic` crate (layer 3). So does
    28	   `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver` (`crates/verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs`, 2122
    29	   lines), the TypeScript-style module resolver wrongly homed in the scheduler/tsgo-dependent
    30	   `verter_workspace` crate today. This is a multi-crate structural move touching `verter_session`'s
    31	   module tree, `verter_workspace`'s module tree, `verter_semantic`'s Cargo.toml dependency edges, and
    32	   the landed dependency-layers closure guard — not a `pub(crate)` facade behind which nothing moves.
    33	2. **The `NeedInputs`/`AttemptOutcome` cutover is full-coverage, not a first cut.** Every non-flow
    34	   `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
    35	   batched outcome — not just the two `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` call sites the prior
    36	   draft scoped it to. TypeInfo projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` today
    37	   (`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`), so "module/import resolution only"
    38	   was never even a clean existing boundary to cut at.
    39	
    40	Effort and breadth are not reasons to shrink this (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning: "Time constraints,
    41	implementation size, migration breadth... are not valid reasons to weaken the design"). The charter
    42	states the true scope instead of preserving the five-line framing that would mislead whoever picks this
    43	up. C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
    44	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and `verter_workspace::resolver` — into the
    45	two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a `ModuleResolverCore` that owns
    46	TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow `TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node
    47	traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution, relation/inference, effective typing,
    48	recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and exactness/completeness propagation. Neither
    49	target type exists in code today; both names describe roles the current tree already plays under
    50	different names, in the wrong crate, with the wrong I/O coupling. C1 does not invent new resolution
    51	semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be identical to
    52	today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code (crate, not just module), how
    53	many duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform
    54	I/O directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
    55	
    56	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
    57	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
    58	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
    59	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions, even
    60	though (per the full-coverage ruling) the *plumbing* around every call into them now must support
    61	`AttemptOutcome`. It owns convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, physical crate
    62	placement, and full-coverage batched/resumable load outcomes so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume
    63	the same kernel a blocking lifecycle consumes today.
    64	
    65	## Sequencing
    66	
    67	C1's predecessors (`A6`, `B1`, `B2`) are all `ACCEPTED`; C1 is dependency-eligible now
    68	(`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:594`, `status = "READY"`). The program executes
    69	one block at a time, and the ledger's `current_block` is `BV1`, `status = "IN_PROGRESS"`
    70	(`program-state.toml:22,510-513`). **C1 dispatch follows BV1's landing.** This charter does not propose
    71	running C1 in parallel with BV1 or with any other in-flight block.
    72	
    73	## Intent Contract
    74	
    75	**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
    76	the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
    77	compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
    78	Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
    79	`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation), by omission (no lifecycle exists
    80	yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), and by the wrong crate holding the kernel at all (a session-tier
    81	crate that already depends on the compiler, so nothing compiler-tier can embed it without a cycle) — not
    82	by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added
    83	without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.
    84	
    85	**Required observable outcomes.**
    86	- A module/name/type/relation query issued through `HostResolverContext`, `SessionResolverContext`, or
    87	  (once added) an I/O-free project-capable context returns bit-identical `SemanticNodeId`/resolved-surface
    88	  results for the same source content, project configuration, and query, modulo the outcome shape
    89	  (blocking-complete vs. `NeedInputs`).
    90	- A resolver-tier operation that needs a not-yet-loaded dependency and runs under an I/O-free environment
    91	  returns `AttemptOutcome::NeedInputs(LoadSet)` (per `contracts/input-loading.md` §2, §4) instead of
    92	  panicking, blocking, or fabricating a partial answer — for **every** non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/
    93	  `TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt, not a subset.
    94	- `verter_semantic`'s production dependency closure contains neither `verter_workspace`,
    95	  `verter_session`, `verter_scheduler`, nor `verter_tsgo_api` on any target — this closes debt row A5-DD1
    96	  by *deleting* the exception, not widening it (`crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/
    97	  workspace_dependency_layers.rs:118-127`, the `ratified_upward_exceptions()` row keyed
    98	  `"verter_semantic"`).
    99	- `resolver_core`, `resolver_store`'s immutable observation types, `project_semantic_dispatch`, and
   100	  `ModuleResolverCore` (the relocated `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver`) physically live in
   101	  `verter_semantic`. `verter_compiler` can depend on the converged kernel directly — it already does
   102	  (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`, `verter_semantic = { path = "../verter_semantic" }`) — with no
   103	  new edge and no cycle.
   104	- A new capability-limited, immutable **observation interface**, defined inside `verter_semantic`, does
   105	  **not** extend today's `ResolverContext` and cannot name, hold, or return `VerterHost` or the
   106	  scheduler — not because a marker says so, but because `verter_semantic`'s crate dependency closure
   107	  makes those types structurally unnameable from inside it.
   108	- The sealed `ResolverContext` trait (relocated to `verter_semantic`) has exactly as many
   109	  production-reachable implementors as there are genuinely distinct blocking lifecycles; a lifecycle that
   110	  cannot resolve (e.g. a bare host with no request/session binding) is a compile-time impossibility for
   111	  resolver-tier call sites, not a documented runtime `panic!`.
   112	
   113	**Forbidden observable outcomes.**
   114	- A second implementation of `SemanticQueryApi::execute`, `execute_relate`, `shallow_lower_type_expr`, a
   115	  second struct owning a `RelationMemo` or the semantic node map (the existing Authority-uniqueness
   116	  contract, `.claude/skills/type-resolution/SKILL.md:790-796` — C1 preserves this unchanged across the
   117	  crate move).
   118	- A converged kernel that reads live, un-snapshotted host state at validation time (defeats "immutable
   119	  observation views").
   120	- A lifecycle-specific answer: the same query returning a different resolved type, a different route, or
   121	  a different completeness verdict depending on which `ResolverContext`/observation-interface implementor
   122	  served it, for identical inputs.
   123	- A blocking wait introduced on the path a future I/O-free lifecycle uses to reach `NeedInputs` — the
   124	  point of the new outcome is that that path never calls `wait_or_drive`/`Condvar::wait`.
   125	- A marker type presented as *the* proof of I/O freedom. Per the ruling on Fork 3, a marker may
   126	  *classify* the observation interface; the proof is that the interface's home crate cannot name the
   127	  host/scheduler types at all. A subtrait of `ResolverContext` is never an acceptable substitute — it
   128	  inherits `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve`/the host escape hatch
   129	  (`resolver_context.rs:780-782,261-266,700-717`) exactly as the rejected draft position did.
   130	- Any resolver-tier operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt that is left blocking-only, with no
   131	  `NeedInputs`-capable path — that is exactly the coverage gap Fork 4's ruling forecloses.
   132	
   133	**Authority/fallback order.** `SemanticQueryKey → ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute → SemanticGraphStore`
   134	remains the sole query-time resolver (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:2206-2214`, the shared choke
   135	point) — unchanged by the crate move. `ResolverContext`/observation-interface implementors are lifecycle
   136	*adapters* over that one authority, never alternate authorities. A resolver-tier operation that cannot
   137	prove a current, coherent view fails closed to a typed non-current miss (`StoreViewRead`'s
   138	`CurrentHostStoreView`/`ColdSeedHostStoreView` split, `.claude/skills/host-session/SKILL.md:678-696`) —
   139	C1 preserves this fail-closed order and must not weaken it while adding the `NeedInputs` outcome
   140	alongside it.
   141	
   142	**Acceptance IDs.**
   143	
   144	| ID | Requirement | Planned test/gate |
   145	|---|---|---|
   146	| C1-AC-1 | Same query, same content, different lifecycle ⇒ same resolved answer | New characterization suite driving one fixed corpus of queries through `HostResolverContext` and `SessionResolverContext` (and the new I/O-free observation interface once added), asserting structural equality of `SemanticNodeId` surfaces, sibling to `resolver_core/*_tests.rs` (relocated) |
   147	| C1-AC-2 | `verter_semantic`'s production closure excludes `verter_workspace`/`verter_session`/`verter_scheduler`/`verter_tsgo_api` on every target, with the A5-DD1 exception row **deleted**, not widened | `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs::workspace_production_closures_never_cross_upward_except_the_recorded_exception` — remove `"verter_semantic"` from `ratified_upward_exceptions()`; any surviving upward edge now hard-fails instead of matching an exception |
   148	| C1-AC-3 | Authority-uniqueness contract holds after the crate move | Existing `project_semantic_dispatch_invariants_tests.rs` + the five-row Authority-uniqueness contract stay green, unmodified in substance, relocated alongside the module they test |
   149	| C1-AC-4 | A resolver-tier call site cannot reach resolution without a request-bound context | `RequestBoundResolverContext` sealed marker (relocated to `verter_semantic`) becomes the *only* production-constructible path once the bare `impl ResolverContext for VerterHost` production rail is deleted (see Legacy Deletions) — `VerterHost` stays in `verter_session` and implements the now-foreign trait for a local type, which the orphan rules permit |
   150	| C1-AC-5 | `AttemptOutcome::{Complete, NeedInputs(LoadSet), Terminal}` covers **every** non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt — full coverage, not one load point | Discharged structurally, not by sampling. Per C1-AC-7 and the Authority/fallback order clause, the observation interface is the *only* surface an I/O-free (C2-shaped) caller can reach a non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation through — `ResolverContext` itself can call `ensure_loaded`/`wait_or_drive`, so it is not usable I/O-free. "Every reachable operation" therefore reduces to "every method on this one finite, closed trait." The trait is defined so every method returns `AttemptOutcome<T>` at the type level (never a bare `T`, `Result<T, _>`, or a call that can block) — a non-conforming method is a compile error at authoring time, not a gap a test could miss. Gate: one exhaustive test double (`impl <ObservationInterface> for TestDouble`) that must implement every trait method to compile; a method added later that does not return `AttemptOutcome<T>` fails to compile at the double, not at a sampled runtime assertion. If a future operation cannot be expressed this way, that is itself a Fork-4-reopening discovery (see Abort/rescope), not a reason to fall back to sampling. |
   151	| C1-AC-6 | Duplicated lifecycle-adapter boilerplate collapses | Diff proof: the ~10 near-identical delegation methods listed under Legacy Deletions shrink to one shared implementation; `HostResolverContext`/`SessionResolverContext` (staying in `verter_session`, implementing the relocated trait) retain only the ~9 genuinely session-specific overrides |

     1	# BV1 — Vue compiler-output conformance train
     2	
     3	**Status:** PROPOSED / LOCKED. **Class:** Framework subsystem.
     4	**Predecessor:** B4.
     5	
     6	## Objective
     7	
     8	Deliver Vue compiler correctness on the final B2–B4 substrate for the exact
     9	`vuejs/core v3.6.0-rc.3` domain.
    10	
    11	## Owned scope
    12	
    13	- Vue-owned semantic model and requested product plans;
    14	- client VDOM and client Vapor generated JavaScript as separate families;
    15	- server/SSR JavaScript and official RC.3 topology;
    16	- script/template assembly; development/production; JavaScript/TypeScript;
    17	- helper/import/call topology, macros, components, directives, events, props,
    18	  attributes, class/style, slots, fragments, Teleport, Suspense, and async setup;
    19	- scoped/slotted metadata, CSS-variable code effects, custom elements, delimiters,
    20	  whitespace/comments, hoisting, handler caching, and binding metadata;
    21	- diagnostics, maps, PublicApi/TSC/declaration/tooling products;
    22	- source-local macro behavior and closed typed demands for imported project data; and
    23	- the complete accepted official-core Vue pack.
    24	
    25	BV1 does not implement Vue runtime code, invent `SSR x Vapor`, use an official
    26	compiler in production, or fulfil project-aware imported macro demands. C3 fulfils
    27	those demands without replacing codegen.
    28	
    29	`FC-TS-001-LOCAL` is BV1's independently closable partition of `FC-TS-001`. It
    30	proves the source-local PublicApi, TSC/TSX, and declaration cells and proves the
    31	BV1 side of the closed BV1→C3 protocol in `C3.md` with typed deterministic
    32	stubs: every demand kind is planned with the specified identity and order, every
    33	`Success` payload is consumed, and every omitted, `NotFound`, `Stale`, or `Error`
    34	result produces the specified typed non-success without partial publication. It
    35	requires no C3 implementation or live project resolver. `FC-TS-001-PROJECT` is
    36	C3's later end-to-end partition; it combines accepted BV1 codegen with the real
    37	project/type substrate and closes `FC-TS-001` for the jointly owned Vue cells.
    38	
    39	## BV0 preservation

    41	BV1's required exits additionally prove that every BV0 correction survives the final
    42	B2–B4 substrate and that the exact BV0 seed pack remains green. BV1 may replace a
    43	BV0 implementation only with an accepted equivalent correction; it may not
    44	reintroduce a corrected defect or convert one into a refusal or tracked divergence.

    48	`FC-VUE-001`, `FC-HYDRATION-001`, `FC-TS-001-LOCAL`, `FC-ATOMIC-001`,
    49	`FC-ZERO-WORK-001`, and applicable `FC-PERF-001` cells pass. Every BV1-owned or

    51	jointly owned project-aware cells remain projection-required until

//! Component metadata extraction from analysis snapshots.
//!
//! Pure analysis-domain types and extraction logic for component-meta.
//! This module does NOT depend on `verter_session` — all resolved data
//! is pre-supplied via [`ComponentMetaInput`].
//!
//! # Ownership boundary
//!
//! - All types in [`ComponentMetaInput`] are owned by `verter_semantic::analysis`
//! - The host constructs the input by projecting from its internal snapshots
//! - [`ComponentMetaAnalysis`] is the analysis-domain result (no serde)
//! - Conversion to transport-facing DTOs happens via `verter_protocol` and its adapter layers

use crate::analysis::types::{
    AnalysisFlags, AnalyzedBinding, AnalyzedExposeField, AnalyzedImport, AnalyzedMacro,
    AnalyzedMacroKind, AnalyzedOptionsApi, AnalyzedPropField, AnalyzedSlotField, ImportBindingKind,
    JsdocTag, StoreUsage, VueApiCallSite,
};
use verter_type_expr::facts::{SemanticTypeSource, SourcePosition};
use verter_type_expr::locators::{AuthoredBodyLocator, MacroPayloadLocator};
use verter_type_expr::{
    AuthoredSourceMint, AuthoredTypeEvidence, PublicationPolicy, ResolutionDiagnostic,
    ResolutionDiagnosticKind, ResolutionExactness, ResolutionProvenance, ResolvedTypeAuthority,
    ResolvedTypeOutcome, TypeExprScope, TypePublication,
};
/// The authored SOURCE of an analyzer field's payload position: the
/// content-free locator wrapped as the four-source `Authored` arm. Consumers
/// demand the typed body through the shared dispatch from it.
fn authored_payload_source(payload: Option<&MacroPayloadLocator>) -> Option<SemanticTypeSource> {
    payload.map(|locator| {
        SemanticTypeSource::Authored(AuthoredBodyLocator::MacroPayload(locator.clone()))
    })
}

/// The authored source POSITION of an analyzer field's payload: the stamped
/// authored locator when the analyzer recorded one, else the PROVEN
/// unannotated schema absence — the analyzer's payload slot IS the authored
/// annotation record, so its absence is structural (an array-form emit, a
/// runtime prop, an untyped binding), never a failure.
fn authored_payload_position(payload: Option<&MacroPayloadLocator>) -> SourcePosition {
    authored_payload_source(payload)
        .map(SourcePosition::Present)
        .unwrap_or_else(SourcePosition::unannotated)
}

fn authored_type_evidence(
    payload: Option<&MacroPayloadLocator>,
    text: Option<&str>,
) -> Option<AuthoredTypeEvidence> {
    // SAFETY: this helper is the analyzer-row producer join: `payload` and
    // `text` are read from the same `Analyzed*Field`.
    let mint = unsafe { AuthoredSourceMint::new_unchecked() };
    Some(AuthoredTypeEvidence::from_macro_payload(
        &mint,
        payload?,
        std::sync::Arc::from(text?),
    ))
}

fn exactness_from_expansion(
    metadata: Option<&crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpansionMetadata>,
    position: &SourcePosition,
) -> ResolutionExactness {
    metadata.map_or_else(
        || match position.present() {
            Some(
                SemanticTypeSource::Closed(_)
                | SemanticTypeSource::Projected(_)
                | SemanticTypeSource::Synthesized(_),
            ) => ResolutionExactness::ExactConcrete,
            Some(SemanticTypeSource::Authored(_) | SemanticTypeSource::SyntheticSlotBinding(_)) => {
                ResolutionExactness::ExactSymbolic
            }
            None => ResolutionExactness::Incomplete,
        },
        |metadata| match metadata.exactness {
            crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpansionExactness::ExactConcrete => {
                ResolutionExactness::ExactConcrete
            }
            crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpansionExactness::ExactSymbolic => {
                ResolutionExactness::ExactSymbolic
            }
            crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpansionExactness::Incomplete => {
                ResolutionExactness::Incomplete
            }
    )
}

/// A present source, else the PROVEN unannotated schema absence. Used at
/// the extraction fallbacks whose `None` structurally means "this position
/// carries no semantic annotation" (untyped bindings, unevaluated exposures,
/// display-only positions) — REQUIRED-position failures never flow through
/// these fallbacks (they arrive as already-classified `Failed` positions on
/// the evaluated lanes).
fn present_or_unannotated(source: Option<SemanticTypeSource>) -> SourcePosition {
    source
        .map(SourcePosition::Present)
        .unwrap_or_else(SourcePosition::unannotated)
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Input view
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/// One host-resolved prop row: the prop analysis field plus the member
/// VALUE's session-resolved SOURCE POSITION — the prop-type authority the
/// extraction publishes (the flat evaluated lanes contribute metadata only).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ResolvedPropInput {
    /// The prop analysis field.
    pub field: AnalyzedPropField,
    /// The member value's published source position.
    pub authority: ResolvedTypeAuthority,
    pub authored_evidence: Option<AuthoredTypeEvidence>,
    /// Typed callable role established by the session resolver.
    pub callable_role: verter_type_expr::PropCallableRole,
}

/// One host-resolved emit row: the emit analysis field plus the payload's
/// session-resolved SOURCE POSITION — the emit-payload authority the
/// extraction publishes (the flat evaluated lanes contribute metadata only).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ResolvedEmitInput {
    /// Resolver-minted opaque producer/name-arm identity.
    pub id: verter_type_expr::facts::ResolvedEmitOccurrenceId,
    /// Event-name literal arm.
    pub name: String,
    /// Exact authored producer span when available.
    pub span: verter_span::Span,
    /// Display-only payload type.
    pub payload_type: Option<String>,
    /// Exact authored payload locator when available.
    pub payload: Option<verter_type_expr::locators::MacroPayloadLocator>,
    /// Scope paired with [`Self::payload_type`].
    pub payload_expr_scope: Option<TypeExprScope>,
    /// Authored producer description.
    pub description: Option<String>,
    /// Authored producer JSDoc tags.
    pub tags: Vec<crate::analysis::types::JsdocTag>,
    /// The payload's published source position.
    pub payload_source: SourcePosition,
    /// Atomic payload publication owned by this occurrence.
    pub payload_publication: TypePublication,
    /// Producer-owned callable return publication. Property/event-map rows use
    /// the implicit `void` return and carry `None`.
    pub return_publication: Option<TypePublication>,
    /// Scope used to raise [`Self::return_publication`]'s selected source.
    pub return_publication_scope: Option<TypeExprScope>,
}

/// One host-resolved expose row: the expose analysis field plus the member
/// VALUE's session-resolved SOURCE POSITION — the exposed-type authority the
/// extraction publishes for type-argument surface members.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ResolvedExposeInput {
    /// The expose analysis field.
    pub field: AnalyzedExposeField,
    /// The member value's published source position.
    pub type_source: SourcePosition,
}

/// One host-resolved script binding's whole-return reactive-wrapper role.
///
/// The session resolves the role of a composable call's AUTHORED return
/// annotation on demand, through the one shared type-resolution engine, and
/// hands the closed typed answer to the extraction. `binding_index` addresses
/// [`ComponentMetaInput::bindings`] positionally; a binding with no row was
/// never demanded (a distinct state from a demanded-and-degraded row, which
/// carries `ReactiveWrapperRole::Unresolved { reason }`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ResolvedBindingReactivityInput {
}

fn extract_exposed_from_macro(
    macro_index: usize,
    mac: &AnalyzedMacro,
    resolved: Option<&ResolvedMacroInput>,
    bindings: &[AnalyzedBinding],
    evaluated: Option<&crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedComponentTypes>,
    out: &mut Vec<ExposedAnalysis>,
) {
    for field in &mac.expose_fields {
        // Mixed-form precedence: an authored object-literal exposure keeps
        // its own (binding-derived) source; the NORMALIZED type-argument
        // surface row only fills what the literal form does not provide (the
        // flat evaluated lane contributes metadata only).
        let resolved_field = resolved.and_then(|resolved| {
            resolved
                .exposed
                .iter()
                .find(|candidate| candidate.field.name == field.name)
        });
        let type_source = resolve_exposed_type(&field.name, bindings, evaluated)
            .map(SourcePosition::Present)
            .or_else(|| resolved_field.map(|candidate| candidate.type_source.clone()))
            .unwrap_or_else(SourcePosition::unannotated);
        // Docs pair by name: the object-literal field's own leading JSDoc
        // wins; a `defineExpose<T>({ ... })` member without one inherits the
        // type-argument surface member's span-sliced JSDoc.
        let description = field
            .description
            .clone()
            .or_else(|| resolved_field.and_then(|candidate| candidate.field.description.clone()));
        let tags = if field.tags.is_empty() {
            resolved_field
                .map(|candidate| candidate.field.tags.clone())
                .unwrap_or_default()
        } else {
            field.tags.clone()
        };
        out.push(ExposedAnalysis {
            name: field.name.clone(),
            type_source,
            type_expansion: evaluated
                .and_then(|eval| {
                    eval.bindings
                        .iter()
                        .find(|binding| binding.name == field.name)
                        .map(field_expansion_metadata)
                })
                .or_else(|| {
                    exposed_lane_field(evaluated, macro_index, &field.name)
                        .map(field_expansion_metadata)
                }),
            description,
            tags,
        });
    }
    // `defineExpose<T>()` surface members with no object-literal counterpart
    // publish from the resolved type-argument surface, in surface order,
    // carrying their span-sliced docs and their NORMALIZED member-value
    // source ([`ResolvedExposeInput::type_source`] — the exposed-type
    // authority: the graph-native closed / shallow-ref / projected
    // member-path ladder, or the typed failure for a genuine miss). The
    // object-literal loop above already consumed the name-paired entries, so
    // this appends only the type-argument-only members. The flat evaluated
    // `exposed` lane contributes ONLY expansion metadata.
    let Some(resolved) = resolved else {
        return;
    };
    for candidate in &resolved.exposed {
        if mac
            .expose_fields
            .iter()
            .any(|f| f.name == candidate.field.name)
        {
            continue;
        }
        out.push(ExposedAnalysis {
            name: candidate.field.name.clone(),
            type_source: candidate.type_source.clone(),
            type_expansion: evaluated
                .and_then(|eval| {
                    eval.bindings
                        .iter()
                        .find(|binding| binding.name == candidate.field.name)
                        .map(field_expansion_metadata)
                })
                .or_else(|| {
                    exposed_lane_field(evaluated, macro_index, &candidate.field.name)
                        .map(field_expansion_metadata)
                }),
            description: candidate.field.description.clone(),
            tags: candidate.field.tags.clone(),
        });
    }
}

/// The projector's per-macro `defineExpose` lane entry for
/// `(macro_index, name)` — the join key pairing a type-argument-derived
/// exposure with its projected surface field.
fn exposed_lane_field<'a>(
    evaluated: Option<&'a crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedComponentTypes>,
    macro_index: usize,
    name: &str,
) -> Option<&'a crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedField> {
    evaluated?
        .exposed
        .iter()
        .find(|entry| entry.macro_index == macro_index)?
        .fields
        .iter()
        .find(|field| field.name == name)
}

fn resolve_exposed_type(
    name: &str,
    bindings: &[AnalyzedBinding],
    evaluated: Option<&crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedComponentTypes>,
) -> Option<SemanticTypeSource> {
    if let Some(eval) = evaluated {
        if let Some(f) = eval.bindings.iter().find(|f| f.name == name) {
            return match f.authority.outcome() {
                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Present { source, .. } => Some(source.as_ref().clone()),
                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Absent { .. } | ResolvedTypeOutcome::Failed { .. } => None,
            };
        }
    }
    // `AnalyzedBinding` carries no typed payload position (its raw annotation
    // text is display-only) — an unevaluated exposed binding is an honest
    // untyped `None`, never a fabricated placeholder.
    let _ = bindings;
    None
}

// ── Options API fallback ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Merge the analyzer's parse-domain prop fields with the host-resolved
/// rows into ONE per-macro row set, each carrying its member-value SOURCE.
/// An analyzer-only field's source is its authored payload position (or the
/// PROVEN unannotated absence for a payload-less runtime field); a
/// host-resolved row's `type_source` is the normalized-surface authority and
/// WINS on a same-name merge (the analysis metadata gap-fills through
/// [`merge_prop_field`]).
fn merged_prop_fields(
    mac: &AnalyzedMacro,
    resolved: Option<&ResolvedMacroInput>,
) -> Vec<ResolvedPropInput> {
    let mut rows: Vec<ResolvedPropInput> = mac
        .prop_fields
        .iter()
        .map(|field| {
            let position = authored_payload_position(field.payload.as_ref());
            ResolvedPropInput {
                authority: ResolvedTypeAuthority::from_source_position(
                    &position,
                    exactness_from_expansion(None, &position),
                    ResolutionProvenance::SemanticEvaluator,
                    std::sync::Arc::from([]),
                ),
                authored_evidence: authored_type_evidence(
                    field.payload.as_ref(),
                    field.type_annotation.as_deref(),
                ),
                callable_role: verter_type_expr::PropCallableRole::default(),
                field: field.clone(),
            }
        })
        .collect();
    if let Some(resolved) = resolved {
        for prop in &resolved.props {
            if let Some(existing) = rows

                let mut seen_bindings: rustc_hash::FxHashSet<String> = field
                    .bindings
                    .iter()
                    .map(|binding| binding.name.clone())
                    .collect();
                for binding in &resolved_slot.bindings {
                    if seen_bindings.insert(binding.name.clone()) {
                        field.bindings.push(binding.clone());
                    }
                }

                if field.return_type.is_none() {
                    field.return_type = resolved_slot.return_type.clone();
                }
                if field.description.is_none() {
                    field.description = resolved_slot.description.clone();
                }
                if field.tags.is_empty() {
                    field.tags = resolved_slot.tags.clone();
                }
                field.is_required |= resolved_slot.is_required;
                if let Some(publication) = resolved
                    .slot_return_publications
                    .get(resolved_index)
                    .cloned()
                    .flatten()
                {
                    return_publications[field_index] = Some(publication);
                }
            }

            for (resolved_index, resolved_slot) in resolved.slots.iter().enumerate() {
                if seen_slots.insert(resolved_slot.name.clone()) {
                    fields.push(resolved_slot.clone());
                    return_publications.push(
                        resolved
                            .slot_return_publications
                            .get(resolved_index)
                            .cloned()
                            .flatten()
                            .or_else(|| slot_return_publication_from_field(resolved_slot)),
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }
    MergedSlotFields {
        fields,
        return_publications,
    }
}

fn extract_props_from_options(opts: &AnalyzedOptionsApi, out: &mut Vec<PropAnalysis>) {
    for prop in &opts.props {
        let raw_type = prop
            .type_annotation
            .clone()
            .or_else(|| prop.type_constructor.clone());
        // Prefer the authored `PropType<T>` payload position when available;
        // else fold the primitive runtime constructor to a closed leaf fact
        // (non-primitive constructors carry display text only — `raw_type`).
        let type_source = authored_payload_source(prop.payload.as_ref()).or_else(|| {
            prop.type_constructor.as_ref().and_then(|rt| {
                use verter_type_expr::facts::{ClosedTypeFact, LeafTypeFact};
                use verter_type_expr::PrimitiveName;
                let primitive = match rt.as_str() {
                    "String" => PrimitiveName::String,
                    "Number" => PrimitiveName::Number,
                    "Boolean" => PrimitiveName::Boolean,
                    _ => return None,
                };
                Some(SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(
                    LeafTypeFact::Primitive(primitive),
                )))
            })
        });
        out.push(PropAnalysis {
            name: prop.name.clone(),
            callable_role: verter_type_expr::PropCallableRole::Other,
            publication: publication_from_position(
                &present_or_unannotated(type_source),
                None,
                authored_type_evidence(prop.payload.as_ref(), raw_type.as_deref()),
                ResolutionProvenance::SemanticEvaluator,
            ),
            type_expansion: None,
            // Options API path: no authored companion for the raw display
            // text (the typed source is above).
            required: prop.is_required,
            has_default: prop.has_default,
            default_value: prop.default_value.clone(),
            description: prop.description.clone(),
            tags: prop.tags.clone(),
            // Options API props are explicit author declarations in the
            // `props: { ... }` object on the component's options block —
            // structurally equivalent to a runtime `defineProps({...})`
            // surface (the author wrote the name directly).
            declared_in_macro_type_arg: true,
        });
    }
}
