  1228	                let name = mac.model_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("modelValue").to_owned();
  1229	                let optional = mac
  1230	                    .prop_fields
  1231	                    .first()
  1232	                    .is_none_or(|field| field.is_optional);
  1233	                let scope = match tsc_scope_requirements(
  1234	                    mac,
  1235	                    scope_inventory,
  1236	                    ctx,
  1237	                    dispatch,
  1238	                    owner_canonical,
  1239	                ) {
  1240	                    Ok(scope) => scope,
  1241	                    Err(failure) => return failure.tsc(),
  1242	                };
  1243	                MacroTscOutcome::Complete(MacroTscProjection::Model(TscModelProjection {
  1244	                    name,
  1245	                    optional,
  1246	                    value_type,
  1247	                    anchor: MacroAnchor::Synthesized {
  1248	                        macro_index: macro_index(effective_index),
  1249	                        row: SynthesizedRowKind::ModelProp,
  1250	                    },
  1251	                    scope,
  1252	                }))
  1253	            }
  1254	            _ => unreachable!("codegen macro filter is exhaustive"),
  1255	        }
  1256	    }
  1257	
  1258	    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  1259	    fn project_runtime_props(
  1260	        &self,
  1261	        ctx: &dyn ResolverContext,
  1262	        dispatch: &ProjectSemanticDispatch<'_>,
  1263	        payload: crate::semantic_query::SemanticNodeId,
  1264	        runtime_subject: &BroadRuntimeSubjectLocator,
  1265	        analysis: &ScriptAnalysisSnapshot,
  1266	        mac: &AnalyzedMacro,
  1267	        payload_index: usize,
  1268	        defaults_index: Option<usize>,
  1269	        classify_constructors: bool,
  1270	        counters: &mut VueMacroCodegenCounters,
  1271	        walker_diagnostics: &mut Vec<crate::project_semantic_dispatch::walk::ShallowDiagnostic>,
  1272	    ) -> MacroRuntimeOutcome {
  1273	        let lane = MacroProjectionLane::runtime(classify_constructors);
  1274	        if probe_definitely_non_object_root(dispatch, payload) {
  1275	            return ProjectionFailure::Invalid(MacroInvalidReason::NonObjectRoot).runtime();
  1276	        }
  1277	        counters.root_shallow_demands += 1;
  1278	        let surface = self.project_shallow_surface_graph_only(
  1279	            ctx,
  1280	            dispatch,
  1281	            payload,
  1282	            Arc::from(Vec::<PathSegment>::new().into_boxed_slice()),
  1283	            ProjectionReductionContext::vue_runtime_object_surface(
  1284	                ProjectionMode::Shallow,
  1285	                SurfaceProvenanceContext::MacroTypeArgOwnBody,
  1286	            ),
  1287	            Some(walker_diagnostics),

   512	pub(super) fn authored_emit_order(anchor: MacroAnchor) -> (u8, u32) {
   513	    match anchor {
   514	        MacroAnchor::Authored { member_ordinal, .. } => (0, member_ordinal.get()),
   515	        MacroAnchor::MacroArgument { .. } | MacroAnchor::Synthesized { .. } => (1, 0),
   516	    }
   517	}
   518	
   519	fn push_emit(rows: &mut Vec<RuntimeEmit>, name: &str, anchor: MacroAnchor) {
   520	    if rows.iter().any(|row| row.name == name) {
   521	        return;
   522	    }
   523	    rows.push(RuntimeEmit {
   524	        name: name.to_owned(),
   525	        anchor,
   526	    });
   527	}
   528	
   529	pub(super) fn member_anchor(mac: &AnalyzedMacro, payload_index: usize, name: &str) -> MacroAnchor {
   530	    let Some(ordinal) = mac
   531	        .prop_fields
   532	        .iter()
   533	        .filter(|field| span_is_owned_by_macro(field.span, mac.span))
   534	        .position(|field| field.name == name)
   535	    else {
   536	        return MacroAnchor::MacroArgument {
   537	            macro_index: macro_index(payload_index),
   538	        };
   539	    };
   540	    MacroAnchor::Authored {
   541	        macro_index: macro_index(payload_index),
   542	        member_ordinal: AuthoredMemberOrdinal::new(member_ordinal(ordinal)),
   543	    }
   544	}
   545	
   546	pub(super) fn authored_emit_anchor(
   547	    mac: &AnalyzedMacro,
   548	    payload_index: usize,
   549	    effective_index: usize,
   550	    name: &str,
   551	) -> MacroAnchor {
   552	    let Some(ordinal) = mac
   553	        .emit_fields
   554	        .iter()
   555	        .filter(|field| span_is_owned_by_macro(field.span, mac.span))
   556	        .position(|field| field.name == name)
   557	    else {
   558	        return MacroAnchor::MacroArgument {
   559	            macro_index: macro_index(payload_index),
   560	        };
   561	    };
   562	    MacroAnchor::Authored {
   563	        macro_index: macro_index(effective_index),
   564	        member_ordinal: AuthoredMemberOrdinal::new(member_ordinal(ordinal)),
   565	    }
   566	}
   567	
   568	fn span_is_owned_by_macro(member: verter_span::Span, mac: verter_span::Span) -> bool {
   569	    member.start >= mac.start && member.end <= mac.end
   570	}

   239	///
   240	/// For type params: emit type alias, replace type param in call with alias name.
   241	/// For no-declarator non-no-return macros: prepend `const ___VERTER___xxx=`.
   242	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   243	fn process_standard_macro(
   244	    macro_name: &str,
   245	    var_suffix: &str,
   246	    call_span: Span,
   247	    declarator: Option<&MacroDeclarator<'_>>,
   248	    type_params: Option<&MacroTypeParams>,
   249	    is_no_return: bool,
   250	    ctx: &mut MacroSourceCtx<'_, '_>,
   251	) -> MacroBindingEntry {
   252	    let type_name_str = format!("{}{}_Type", PREFIX, macro_name);
   253	    let auto_var_name = format!("{}{}", PREFIX, var_suffix);
   254	
   255	    let has_type_params = type_params.is_some();
   256	
   257	    // Determine the statement start position for prepending
   258	    let stmt_start = declarator
   259	        .map(|d| ctx.content_start + d.statement_span.start)
   260	        .unwrap_or(ctx.content_start + call_span.start);
   261	
   262	    // Emit type alias for type params
   263	    if let Some(tp) = type_params {
   264	        if ctx.is_jsx {
   265	            // JSX mode: remove the generic type brackets entirely (JS has no generics)
   266	            ctx.out.overwrite(tp.lt_span.start, tp.gt_span.end, "");
   267	        } else {
   268	            let type_text = &ctx.source[tp.type_span.start as usize..tp.type_span.end as usize];
   269	            let needs_prettify = !is_simple_type_reference(type_text);
   270	
   271	            let prefix = if needs_prettify {
   272	                format!(";type {}={}Prettify<", type_name_str, PREFIX)
   273	            } else {
   274	                format!(";type {}=", type_name_str)
   275	            };
   276	            let suffix = if needs_prettify { ">;" } else { ";" };
   277	
   278	            // Move original type content to stmt_start, wrapped with type declaration.
   279	            // This preserves fine-grained sourcemap for hover on individual properties.
   280	            ctx.out.move_wrapped(
   281	                tp.type_span.start,
   282	                tp.type_span.end,
   283	                stmt_start,
   284	                &prefix,
   285	                suffix,

   559	        // SUPPORTED-with-members, never unsupported-because-present. The

   569	                FrameworkSurfaceKind::Slots => mac_kind == AnalyzedMacroKind::DefineSlots,
   570	                FrameworkSurfaceKind::Model => mac_kind == AnalyzedMacroKind::DefineModel,
   571	                FrameworkSurfaceKind::Options => mac_kind == AnalyzedMacroKind::DefineOptions,
   572	                FrameworkSurfaceKind::Expose => mac_kind == AnalyzedMacroKind::DefineExpose,

    71	
    72	## Finding B — root cause
    73	
    74	### The literal error text vs. what actually happens
    75	
    76	`"component-meta output materialization failed at exposed[].type index <N>: the source has no
    77	live graph representation under the request view"` is produced by exactly one place:
    78	`ComponentMetaOutputError`'s `Display` impl for the `UnraisableSource` variant
    79	(`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/output.rs:562-564`). That variant is only reached when
    80	a lane's `SourcePosition` is `Present(source)` **and** the shared raise
    81	(`ProjectSemanticDispatch::raise_semantic_type_source_to_hot_strict`,
    82	`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/semantic_source.rs:428`) returns `Ok(None)`
    83	for a disposition that isn't a legitimate carrier
    84	(`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink.rs:1216-1273`).
    85	
    86	**In every fixture I constructed, the exposed member's `SourcePosition` is never `Present` in
    87	the first place — it is `Absent(SchemaAbsence::Unannotated)`.** Per
    88	`materialize_output_lane_slot` (`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink/envelope.rs:144-171`),
    89	an `Absent` position is a documented, intentional success path: it renders
    90	`missing_source_output_type_expr()` = `TypeExpr::Unknown(UnknownValue::missing_output())`
    91	**with no error at all** (`Ok(missing_source_output_type_expr())`, not
    92	`Err(ComponentMetaOutputFailure::…)`). That is exactly the value my repro observes:
    93	`Unknown(UnknownValue { raw: "", provenance: MissingOutput })`, and `get_component_meta_output`
    94	returns `Ok(Some(..))`, not `Err(..)`.
    95	
    96	So the symptom I can reproduce in-repo is **upstream** of the raise/materialize step the task
    97	brief's hypothesis targeted: the exposed binding never gets a `Present` source at all, so the
    98	strict raise path is never entered and never has a chance to fail loudly.
    99	
   100	### The actual mechanism
   101	
   102	`ExposedAnalysis::type_source` (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs:453-462`)
   103	is set by `resolve_exposed_type` (same file, line 2794):
   104	
   105	```rust
   106	fn resolve_exposed_type(name, bindings, evaluated) -> Option<SemanticTypeSource> {
   107	    if let Some(eval) = evaluated {
   108	        if let Some(f) = eval.bindings.iter().find(|f| f.name == name) {
   109	            return match f.authority.outcome() {
   110	                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Present { source, .. } => Some(source.as_ref().clone()),
   111	                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Absent { .. } | ResolvedTypeOutcome::Failed { .. } => None,
   112	            };
   113	        }
   114	    }
   115	    None   // <-- the name was never even offered
   116	}
   117	```
   118	
   119	For an object-literal `defineExpose({ a, b })` (the common, documented Vue form — as opposed to
   120	the type-argument `defineExpose<T>()` form, which is a separate, working code path through
   121	`meta_resolve/projectors/exposed.rs`), the ONLY way an exposed name reaches
   122	`eval.bindings` is via the general macro-argument-type expansion's **binding-entry admission
   123	gate**:
   124	
   125	`crates/verter_session/src/host_manage/eval_env.rs::component_meta_binding_type_entries`
   126	(lines ~907-956):
   127	
   128	```rust
   129	admitted
   130	    .iter()
   131	    .filter(|binding| {
   132	        ctx.prepared_value_decl(canonical, binding.owner, binding.name.as_ref())
   133	            .is_some_and(|decl| {
   134	                !matches!(
   135	                    decl.type_annotation.classification,
   136	                    verter_type_expr::facts::ValueAnnotationClass::Absent
   137	                )
   138	            })
   139	    })
   140	    .map(|binding| BindingExpansionEntry { name: …, owner: … })
   141	    .collect()
   142	```
   143	
   144	This is a **deliberate, documented gate** ("the `defineExpose` binding-entry NAMES the macro
   145	expander emits … the same has-annotation gate the retired typed-entry list applied") — but it
   146	checks **only** `PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation.classification`. It silently drops any
   147	binding whose type-bearing evidence lives somewhere else on `PreparedValueDecl`:
   148	
   149	- `PreparedValueDecl.signatures: Vec<FunctionSignature>` — a plain `function` **declaration**'s
   150	  type. Confirmed: `function focus(): void {}` still fails even with an explicit return type,
   151	  because a function declaration's type is never carried on `.type_annotation` at all — it's
   152	  structurally a `signatures`-only decl. The gate has no branch for this.
   153	- Whatever carries the type for a `const x = ref(0)` / `const x: Ref<number> = ref(0)`
   154	  initializer. I traced the general variable-declarator lowering
   155	  (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_eval_build.rs::lower_variable_declarator_parts`,
   156	  ~lines 3260-3394) and its `value_type_derives_from_a_call` branch (line 5997) — by that
   157	  reading, `expression_source_offset` should be set for a call-expression initializer, and an
   158	  *explicit* `Ref<number>` annotation should short-circuit straight to
   159	  `ValueAnnotationClass::Direct` via `value_type_annotation_fact`
   160	  (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/fact_projection.rs:78-153`) regardless of the call.
   161	  That did **not** match the observed behavior (still `Absent` even with the explicit
   162	  annotation) — **I could not fully close this gap within budget.** Either
   163	  `lower_variable_declarator_parts` is not actually the code path invoked for `<script setup>`
   164	  top-level bindings in a `.vue` carrier (there may be a separate SFC/framework-specific binding
   165	  lowering that doesn't thread the same annotation/call logic), or `prepared_value_decl`'s
   166	  lookup (`visible_value_binding` / owner resolution) fails to find `count`/`doubled` at all for
   167	  a reason unrelated to annotation classification. Either way, the **admission gate is the
   168	  point where the binding is lost**, confirmed by direct instrumentation (see next section) —
   169	  what I couldn't pin down is which specific upstream producer fails to feed it.
   170	
   171	### Direct evidence (from the diagnostic traces run during this investigation, now folded into
   172	the isolation tests above)
   173	
   174	| Fixture | `exposed[].type_source` |
   175	|---|---|
   176	| `const x: number = 5` | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   177	| `const b: Box<number> = { value: 1 }` (local generic, no call) | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   178	| `const focus: () => void = () => {}` (arrow expr, no call) | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   179	| `const count = ref(0)` (untyped, call init) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   180	| `const count: Ref<number> = ref(0)` (typed, call init) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   181	| `function focus(): void {}` (declaration) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   182	
   183	The pattern is exact and reproducible: **any exposed binding that is either (a) a plain
   184	function declaration, or (b) a `const` whose initializer is a call expression — regardless of
   185	whether it carries an explicit type annotation — is silently dropped before it ever reaches a
   186	`Present` source position.** This covers exactly the two shapes a real-world Options-free Vue 3
   187	component's `defineExpose` almost always uses: exposed methods, and exposed `ref()`/`computed()`
   188	state. That matches the task's four failing real fixtures (methods, refs/computed, full-API,
   189	runtime-props) far better than a raise-time failure would.
   190	
   191	### Contract violated / owner
   192	
   193	This violates the Component-Meta Shallow-By-Default / general "no silent Unknown for a
   194	present-in-source binding" expectation — a `defineExpose`d name that is lexically visible and
   195	has a perfectly good type (inferable from `ref`'s signature, or the function's own signature) is
   196	being treated identically to "the author wrote no type at all." The owning layer is
   197	`verter_session`'s component-meta binding-type-entry admission gate
   198	(`host_manage/eval_env.rs::component_meta_binding_type_entries`) plus, contingent on the
   199	open trace gap above, possibly the variable-declarator/binding lowering that feeds
   200	`PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation` for `<script setup>` scopes. This is **squarely inside
   201	`verter_session`'s existing analysis/expansion pipeline** — a narrow, local fix (make the gate
   202	also admit when `!decl.signatures.is_empty()`, and close the call-expression-initializer gap in
   203	whichever producer is actually in play for SFC bindings). **It does not require C1's
   204	request-view/lifecycle rework** — nothing here is about view identity, request-scoping, or
   205	resolver-caching; it's a pre-existing admission filter dropping legitimate candidates before any
   206	raise/dispatch step is reached.

   229	## Finding C — root cause
   230	
   231	### Reproduction detail
   232	
   233	`defineProps({ label: String, count: Number, enabled: Boolean })` — `label` materializes to
   234	`Unknown(UnknownValue{raw:"", provenance: MissingOutput})`. Same failure class as Finding B:
   235	**`Absent` schema position, silently rendered**, not a raise-time error.
   236	
   237	### Mechanism
   238	
   239	There are two structurally parallel prop-extraction paths in
   240	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs`:
   241	
   242	1. **Options API** (`export default { props: {...} } `) — `extract_props_from_options`
   243	   (line 3023). This path **does** special-case runtime constructors: it reads
   244	   `prop.type_constructor: Option<String>` (populated at parse time in
   245	   `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/options.rs:168-233` from the identifier name `String`/
   246	   `Number`/`Boolean`) and maps it into a real, closed semantic fact:
   247	   ```rust
   248	   let primitive = match rt.as_str() {
   249	       "String" => PrimitiveName::String,
   250	       "Number" => PrimitiveName::Number,
   251	       "Boolean" => PrimitiveName::Boolean,
   252	       _ => return None,
   253	   };
   254	   Some(SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(LeafTypeFact::Primitive(primitive))))
   255	   ```
   256	
   257	2. **Composition API macro** (`defineProps({...})` inside `<script setup>`) — the code path my
   258	   repro exercises — `extract_props_from_macro` (line 1737), non-type-based fallback
   259	   (`mac.is_type_based == false`), which builds each `PropAnalysis.publication` from
   260	   `resolve_prop_type(row, evaluated)` off `row.field`'s **authored payload position**
   261	   (`field.payload: Option<MacroPayloadLocator>`).
   262	
   263	The runtime-constructor recognizer for the macro path,
   264	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs::constructor_to_ts_type` (line 2982), **only
   265	produces a display-only text string** (`AnalyzedPropField.type_annotation: Option<String>` —
   266	explicitly documented elsewhere in this codebase as a display-only passthrough that must never
   267	feed semantic decisions). For the shorthand form (`label: String`) and the bare `type: String`
   268	form, `constructor_to_ts_type`'s result is written **only** to `type_annotation` (display text)
   269	— `field.payload` (the thing `authored_payload_position`/`resolve_prop_type` actually reads to
   270	build a `SemanticTypeSource`) is left `None` unless the author wrote an explicit `X as
   271	PropType<T>` assertion (`has_authored_prop_type_assertion`,
   272	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs:2998-3023`, gated by
   273	`type_expr_scope = has_authored_prop_type.then(...)` at line 3139-3140).
   274	
   275	So: for the ordinary, most-common `defineProps({ label: String })` runtime-declaration form,
   276	**no typed semantic source is ever constructed at all** — only a throwaway display string. The
   277	field's `SourcePosition` therefore resolves as genuinely `Absent`, and the output sink correctly
   278	(per its own contract) renders that as `Unknown`.
   279	
   280	### Why optionality survives but the type doesn't
   281	
   282	`required`/`has_default` in `extract_props_from_macro`'s fallback loop
   283	(`component_meta.rs:1827-1846`) is computed independently, from `field.is_optional` (a bool set
   284	directly from whether `required: true` was seen in `macros.rs::extract_prop_fields_from_runtime`,
   285	line 3055/3116-3120) and `default_keys`/`default_values` — none of which route through
   286	`field.payload`/`resolve_prop_type` at all. That's a disjoint, working computation, which is
   287	exactly why the task's observed behavior is "optionality survives, primitive type is lost."
   288	
   289	### Contract violated / owner
   290	
   291	This is a **parity gap between the Options-API and Composition-API (macro) prop-extraction
   292	paths** inside `verter_semantic::analysis` — the Options API already does the correct thing
   293	(map a recognized runtime constructor identifier to a closed primitive semantic fact at the
   294	analyzer/extraction layer, not at the output seam); the macro path never got (or lost) the
   295	equivalent. This is **not** a case of "no source exists for this position" — the source (the
   296	literal identifier `String`) is right there in the AST; the analyzer captures it as display text
   297	and then discards the semantic identity. The correct fix location is the same layer the Options
   298	API path already uses correctly: `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs`'s
   299	`extract_prop_fields_from_runtime` (or a shared helper it and `analysis/options.rs` both call)
   300	should mint a `SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(LeafTypeFact::Primitive(...)))` (or
   301	populate an equivalent typed locator on `AnalyzedPropField`) for a recognized runtime
   302	constructor, mirroring what `extract_props_from_options` already does — **not** a hard-coded
   303	string-to-primitive mapping at the final output seam (which the task's hard prohibitions
   304	correctly rule out).
   305	
   306	This is **fixable under the current architecture** — it's a straightforward analyzer-layer
   307	parity fix between two already-existing, structurally-similar extraction functions in the same
   308	file family. No request-view/lifecycle rework is implicated.
   309	
   310	### What I could not determine for Finding C
   311	
   312	- I did not check whether the same gap applies to the `{ type: String, default: '...' }`
   313	  expanded object form specifically (vs. the shorthand `label: String` form) — the code reads as
   314	  identically affected (both write only to `type_annotation` via the same `constructor_to_ts_type`
   315	  call, `macros.rs:3110-3114`), but I did not add a fixture for it.
   316	- I did not check whether arrays of constructors (`label: [String, Number]`) or `PropType<T>`
   317	  the CORRECT way already work end-to-end (they should, per the `has_authored_prop_type`
   318	  branch, which does populate `type_expr_scope`/a payload position) — this is consistent with
   319	  the code but I did not add a positive-control fixture proving it in-repo.
   320	- I did not check whether this same defect surfaces identically for `defineModel` or Options-API
   321	  `props: [...]` (array shorthand) — out of scope for the reported fixtures but worth a sweep
   322	  before landing a fix.
   323

    11	
    12	## Context — why this is bigger than program.md's five lines
    13	
    14	`program.md:191-197` gives C1 five lines: converge two logical owners, preserve resolution semantics,
    15	use immutable observation views, return batched `NeedInputs`, exclude flow. Read literally that sounds
    16	like an in-place refactor. **It is not.** The four rulings resolve every genuine fork in the direction
    17	that costs the most, and the charter says so plainly rather than understating it:
    18	
    19	1. **This is a real crate extraction, now, not a deferred one.** `resolver_core` (`pub mod`, 59 files —
    20	   including `component_meta/` (6 files) and `component_meta_query_engine/` (14 files): verified, neither
    21	   holds a `&VerterHost`/`Arc<VerterHost>` field or parameter in production code, only doc-comment mentions
    22	   and `#[cfg(test)]` `VerterHost::new` fixture construction identical to the pattern already accepted for
    23	   `resolver_core`'s own top-level `*_tests.rs` files, so both subdirectories move with the rest of the
    24	   wildcard, not a carve-out — see the convergence map below),
    25	   the private `resolver_store` module, and the `pub(crate)` `project_semantic_dispatch` module —
    26	   all three currently living inside `verter_session` (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:332,341-344`)
    27	   — physically relocate into the existing `verter_semantic` crate (layer 3). So does
    28	   `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver` (`crates/verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs`, 2122
    29	   lines), the TypeScript-style module resolver wrongly homed in the scheduler/tsgo-dependent
    30	   `verter_workspace` crate today. This is a multi-crate structural move touching `verter_session`'s
    31	   module tree, `verter_workspace`'s module tree, `verter_semantic`'s Cargo.toml dependency edges, and
    32	   the landed dependency-layers closure guard — not a `pub(crate)` facade behind which nothing moves.
    33	2. **The `NeedInputs`/`AttemptOutcome` cutover is full-coverage, not a first cut.** Every non-flow
    34	   `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
    35	   batched outcome — not just the two `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` call sites the prior
    36	   draft scoped it to. TypeInfo projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` today
    37	   (`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`), so "module/import resolution only"
    38	   was never even a clean existing boundary to cut at.
    39	
    40	Effort and breadth are not reasons to shrink this (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning: "Time constraints,
    41	implementation size, migration breadth... are not valid reasons to weaken the design"). The charter
    42	states the true scope instead of preserving the five-line framing that would mislead whoever picks this
    43	up. C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
    44	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and `verter_workspace::resolver` — into the
    45	two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a `ModuleResolverCore` that owns
    46	TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow `TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node
    47	traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution, relation/inference, effective typing,
    48	recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and exactness/completeness propagation. Neither
    49	target type exists in code today; both names describe roles the current tree already plays under
    50	different names, in the wrong crate, with the wrong I/O coupling. C1 does not invent new resolution
    51	semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be identical to
    52	today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code (crate, not just module), how
    53	many duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform
    54	I/O directly, and where the crate boundary sits.

    56	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
    57	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
    58	publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
    59	`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions, even
    60	though (per the full-coverage ruling) the *plumbing* around every call into them now must support
    61	`AttemptOutcome`. It owns convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, physical crate
    62	placement, and full-coverage batched/resumable load outcomes so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume

    18	## The defect (release blocker, regression vs published beta.3)
    19	
    20	Production VDOM template codegen panics at
    21	`crates/verter_compiler/src/template/code_gen/types.rs:712`:
    22	`overwrite_segmented precondition violated at [0,21): ReplacedContentSplit { offset: 0 }`
    23	
    24	## Established root cause — reproduced in-repo, instrumented, confirmed
    25	
    26	Full report: `<SESSION_SCRATCH>/scratchpad/FINDING-A-ROOT-CAUSE.md`. A reproducing test exists at
    27	`crates/verter_compiler/tests/cases/vdom_root_static_class_comment_prefix_panic.rs` (in the
    28	investigation worktree, not landed): the bug SFC fails red with the identical panic; three negative
    29	controls (no static class / no comment / dev mode) pass, matching every known ablation.
    30	
    31	Confirmed failing path: **`find_sole_containing_original` returns `None`** — NOT the
    32	`anchored_present` branch (that machinery is unreached; no template-codegen call site uses
    33	`append_left`/`prepend_right`/`append_right`).
    34	
    35	Two producers write overlapping subranges of the template header:
    36	
    37	1. `visit_comment` → `comment::process_comment`, walker-ordered BEFORE `leave_template`, does an
    38	   unconditional plain `overwrite(comment.start, comment.end, "")` on `[10,18)` when
    39	   `comments: false`. Lands in the `overwrites` channel.
    40	2. `leave_template`'s single-root block path, needing to carry hoisted-static-class anchors, does
    41	   `overwrite_or_root_prefix_segmented` on `[root.tag_open.start, child.start) = [0,21)` — a SUPERSET
    42	   structurally containing producer 1's range. Lands in `segmented_overwrites`.
    43	
    44	`CodeGenOutput::apply_to` flushes `overwrites` before `segmented_overwrites` unconditionally, so by
    45	the time the segmented overwrite runs its target is no longer one untouched `Original` chunk and the
    46	(correctly strict) precondition fires. Both conditions are individually necessary and jointly sufficient.
    47	
    48	## The investigator's recommended repair
    49	
    50	Merge ownership: teach `leave_template` — which already computes the drained leading-children set — to
    51	suppress/absorb the independent comment-strip overwrite for any comment falling inside its own claimed
    52	header range, since the segmented prefix's synthetic content already elides those bytes. This leaves the
    53	strict single-chunk precondition intact rather than weakening it.
    54	
    55	## Decide
    56	
    57	1. **Is that the correct repair, or is a different class better?** Alternatives on the table: reorder so
    58	   the segmented overwrite consumes the original range first; narrow one overwrite to avoid overlap;
    59	   represent an edit as an anchored insertion rather than a replacement; carry the original segment
    60	   through the combined operation; eliminate duplicate ownership of the region. Rule, with reasoning
    61	   grounded in the transform-ownership contracts — not in "what stops the panic".
    62	2. **Is the flush order in `CodeGenOutput::apply_to` itself the defect?** An unconditional
    63	   `overwrites`-then-`segmented_overwrites` flush means any producer pair with this shape collides.

   103	>
   104	> This banner is removed when the program completes and the target architecture is described here directly.
   105	
   106	Verter = a Vue compiler + Language Server Protocol (LSP) implementation. Converts Vue Single File Components (SFCs) to valid TSX (TypeScript type-checks them) and compiles templates to optimized render functions. Unlike Volar, Verter generates real valid TSX, not virtual files.
   107	
   108	Hybrid Rust + TypeScript monorepo: Rust crates own carrier parsing, runtime and IDE code generation, the shared semantic session, and the LSP server (`verter_lsp` binary, stdio); TypeScript packages provide editor integration, TypeScript-provider adapters, protocol bindings, and bundler orchestration.
   109	
   110	## Architecture
   111	
   112	Detailed module reference, key files, and implementation specifics live in domain skills: `/type-resolution`, `/type-cache-architecture`, `/component-meta`, `/compiler-codegen`, `/host-session`, `/architecture`.
   113	
   114	### Shared Optimized Codebase (CRITICAL)
   115	
   116	Verter is one shared optimized codebase, not separate semantic implementations per consumer.
   117	
   118	- Improvements land in the lowest reusable owner crate that can correctly serve all consumers.
   119	- `verter_session` + shared workspace/VFS integration are the authority for host-backed loading, invalidation, dependency tracking, cache reuse.
   120	- `verter_semantic` + `verter_compiler` own reusable semantics, lowering, codegen.
   121	- `verter_session::resolver_core` owns the host-backed resolver stack + type-resolution orchestration.
   122	- `verter_audit` is the leaf observability substrate (depends only on `verter_span`, no back-edge; lower crates emit through `current_observer()` (TLS) without knowing whether a `HostAuditRuntime` is installed); the concrete host runtime lives in `verter_session` — full ownership inventory in `/audit-infrastructure`.
   123	- `verter_protocol` owns transport-facing schema DTOs; `verter_ffi` remains the thin native/WASM adapter layer.
   124	- Consumer packages (`@verter/component-meta`, LSP, MCP, unplugin, playground) consume the shared substrate, not their own semantic forks.
   125	
   126	Architectural consequence:
   127	
   128	- A perf/correctness fix found in one surface is implemented in the shared owner layer whenever the behavior is reusable.
   129	- Consumer-local wrappers stay thin and do not bypass shared parsing, analysis, resolution, or cache ownership.
   130	
   131	**Exactly one type-resolution engine.** `SemanticQueryKey` → `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute` → `SemanticGraphStore`, five query modes (`Identity`/`Navigate`/`Shallow`/`Expanded`/`Skeleton`) — the SOLE query-time type resolver. OXC is the syntax/lowering front-end ONLY (declaration bodies lower to `TypeExpr` lazily on first semantic demand through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot — the `DeclBodyMemo` owned by `IndexedReady`); OXC must never resolve types at query time. Any second query-time resolution path — a parallel `resolve_type` engine, a per-surface walker, a re-parse-and-resolve, an OXC element/frontier resolver — is a rule violation: delete it, route through the shared resolver. Two engines diverge; divergence is the bug/hang class.
   132	
   133	**Audit infrastructure:** Rust-first deterministic per-request observability for every audited `VerterHost` entry-point (component-meta, type-resolution, compile, analyze, workspace ops, LSP handlers, MCP tools, bundler batches). TS bindings in `packages/types/audit.generated.ts`; opt-in via `HostConfig::audit_enabled + footprint_capture`. See `/audit-infrastructure` and [`docs/audit-footprint/`](docs/audit-footprint/).
   134	
   135	Guards: `verter_audit_no_upward_deps`, `audit_substrate_isolation`, `audit_observer_single_accessor`. The former single-engine `no_new_*` shrinking-ledger scanners retired with the deleted parser-owned `type_surface` engine; the single-engine invariant is now held structurally (the compiler consumes only the dependency-neutral macro DTO) plus the Vue macro boundary suite registered under "Vue Macro Semantic Boundary" in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`.
   136	
   137	### Build Philosophy (CRITICAL)
   138	
   139	Same end-state philosophy as `binary-exploring-lamport.md`. Core rules:
   140	
   141	1. Read, parse, shallow-process, cache each canonical file once per content hash through one shared host path.
   142	2. Store the full shallow symbol inventory up front, then process only requested items on demand.
   143	3. Same-file closure stays local to the owning file.
   144	4. Cross-file deepening happens in one place only, one import level at a time.
   145	5. The builder/solver reads only from cached lookup state; it does not reopen file loading or routing.
   146	6. The design is demand-driven and query-scoped.
   147	7. The final implementation lands as one clean cutover, not a merged dual-path transition.
   148	8. Component-meta, LSP, MCP, and other host-backed consumers share the same file-ready/read/parse/shallow-process lifecycle.
   149	
   150	These are architecture rules, not optimization hints. On conflict, fix the owner layer or delete the legacy path rather than preserve a second read/parse/resolution flow.
   151	
   152	Guards: `no_thread_local_oxc_caches`, `no_direct_oxc_parser_calls_outside_scheduler_path`, `recursion_budget_invariant_across_module_boundary`.
   153	
   154	### Shallow File Processing Core Invariant (CRITICAL)
   155	
   156	The shallow file process is a core architectural invariant and must be preserved. When a canonical file is processed, the host stores its shallow symbol inventory once; that inventory is the authoritative index later stages query.
   157	
   158	Shallow state must classify and retain at minimum: imports; exports and reexports; type declarations; interfaces; enums; classes; variables/constants; functions/method signatures; `typeof`-relevant value declarations; local symbol dependency edges; cross-file dependency edges.
   159	
   160	Design rule: processing a file means collecting and indexing its symbols, not eagerly evaluating them; later stages look up the indexed items they need and process only those on demand; no stage rescans the raw file to rediscover symbols shallow processing already captured. Performance: very high performance comes from targeted demand after broad shallow indexing, not repeated partial reparsing.
   161	
   162	Core invariants (full architectural-target detail: `/type-resolution` → IndexedReady Target Contract + Cache Population Target Contract):
   163	
   164	- Canonical post-parse artifact = `IndexedReady`: a shallow declaration INDEX plus body locators, NOT a body store. Eagerly it carries canonical imports/exports, top-level symbol names/kinds, declaration spans, source-order contributor grouping, type-parameter names, syntactic member headers, and augmentation inventory — all safe for host-owned `Send + Sync` caches. Declaration BODIES lower only on first semantic demand through the shared lazy body service (the content-addressed `DeclBodyMemo` + scheduler-side `DeclLoweringService` retained-parse workers); publishing an artifact lowers ZERO declaration bodies. Component-meta and later analysis layers both build from it; symbol expansion populates and reuses the same shared resolver caches — no separate expansion paths.
   165	- Parse each live file version once; the lazy lowering service RETAINS the parse snapshot on its worker shard (keyed `(canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash)`) so body demands reuse it instead of re-parsing per touch. Transient OXC parse arenas stay per-file/per-version and never leak into host-owned shared caches — jobs borrow the retained AST on the worker and return owned typed IR.
   166	- The declaration-body **hot READ path is handle-native at the one migrated graph-backed site** (`lower_decl_body_to_node`) through `decl_body_hot_ref`; prepared declarations and `LoweredValueDecl` are fact+locator `NoTypeExpr`, and `LoweredTypeDecl.body` is content-free. The two former stored type-parameter `TypeExpr` pockets are CLOSED (the type-parameter-bound confinement block): `LoweredTypeDecl` is wholly `NoTypeExpr` — the stored full `type_parameters: Vec<TypeParam>` is gone; the `narrow_type_parameters` mirror (name + ordinal + content-free bound locators) is the sole stored authority, consumed by the prepared-decl builder and the external frontier (which content-free re-anchors the mirror's bound slots to the frontier symbol, preserving `export default`), while the locator/binder deref uses the mirror for ordinal/name/bound-presence authority and re-borrows bound CONTENT + the full sibling frame lease-only from the retained snapshot (`transient_type_parts`). `TypeParamBinding` is likewise shrunk to the content-free `(name, ordinal)` fact pair (`NoTypeExpr`): its `<script setup generic="…">` bounds are re-borrowed at query time through ONE artifact-local transient producer over the pinned `IndexedReady` and lowered by ONE dispatch helper shared by both content readers, with a missing/stale re-borrow failing as a typed cache-suppressed miss, never a bound-free fabricated binder. The residual-reader ledger is not a terminal-zero mechanism: `ProducerLowering` is permanent transient ingress, the five `GraphFreeDto` rows remain named until the separate producer-boundary-confinement cutover, and a hot consumer must never take `HotTypeRef → TypeExpr → semantic decision`.
   167	- Navigation stays narrower than expansion: walking `A['c']['full']['bar']` navigates intermediate hops and expands only the terminal requested projection unless limited normalization is required to continue.
   168	- Generic substitutions are semantic meaning: navigation/expansion operate on instantiated types; cache keys include the relevant substitutions/type arguments.
   169	- Navigators stay non-owning (choose the next hop, non-owning normalization only); reusable semantic work enters through the shared query API, not a private drill-down path. The shared semantic layer is keyed by semantic query identity and stores immutable semantic data or ids — never borrowed AST pointers or retained parser arenas.
   170	- Completion fence: top-level live-host results record touched dependency facts, revalidate before publish, retry at most 3 times on mid-flight changes; never warm shared caches with torn provisional results; cancelled, superseded, interrupted, budget-exceeded, or partial results are never promoted warm.
   171	- Waiters on in-flight work block cooperatively, never busy-spin; same-path recursion never self-awaits.
   172	- Cache population is path-independent (same result from different entry points → same shared entry); broader successful results may backfill only the narrower entries they actually satisfied; narrower results must not pretend broader work is cached.
   173	- Final payload caches hand out immutable `Arc` values; any backend preserving concurrency, size bounds, validation semantics is fine.
   174	
   175	Guards: `audit_publishes_member_edge_with_published_field_provenance_at_macro_boundaries`, `macro_impacting_constructs_fail_lowering_not_silent_skip`, `indexed_ready_publish_lowers_zero_decl_bodies`, `resolve_unrelated_symbol_lowers_only_demanded_decl`, `lazy_decl_body_singleflight_lowers_once`, `no_indexed_ready_eval_env_or_type_decl_body_storage`, `emit_parse_facts_never_hashes_decl_bodies`.
   176	
   177	**Project-global cache (final state):** `VerterHost` owns a single `ProjectTypeStore` accessed via `.project_type_store()` — the sole shared cache graph: `FileArtifactStore`, `AnalysisReadyDb`, the rehomed `RouteDb`, `OwnerImportSurfaceDb`, `ComponentMetaResultDb<ComponentMetaAnalysis>`, `MaterializeStructureDb`, `SemanticGraphStore` (which also owns the Vue macro resolution artifacts — the former `ResolvedNamedTypesDb`), `ShapeCacheDb`, `FlowSliceStores` (the flow-return substrate's per-function graph/slice artifact stores), and the `IntrinsicRegistry`. `IndexedReady` is the single canonical post-parse artifact (the former `ModuleFactsDb` is retired). Validated cache writes record a `ReadSetSignature.facts` fact signature (the path-precise fact-tracer observation set) — the sole cache-validity rail, revalidated against the live `StoreView` on every warm hit. The `StoreViewValidationToken` is the complete reuse/validity oracle; the singleflight LANE identity is the narrower `external_supersession_fingerprint` (reuse-oracle = full token; lane-identity = external fingerprint). See `/host-session` (store-view token dimensions, token-advance rules, lane identity, singleflight, `RequestStoreView`/`CanonicalCompletionOverlay`, handle-backed dims), `/component-meta` (`get_component_meta` final-result flow, `resolve_owner_direct_import`, `materialize_component_meta_structure`, the `ShapeCacheDb` per-member route, `reduce_published_field_types` / sink-private `reduce_field_value_node`), `/type-cache-architecture` (admission, retired split stores), and `/type-resolution` (`execute_cooperative` dedup, `SemanticNodeData::VueMacroElements` hot path, `IntrinsicRegistry::lookup`).
   178	
   179	### Canonical Dependency Cache Rule (CRITICAL)
   180

   600	notes = "Fragment-based assembly, atomic publication and typed all-or-nothing refusal for Vue main-module compilation. Identity independently verified: linear fast-forward 664cab091 to 6a14dbe5f with zero merges, candidate equals accepted so no landing-equivalence proof is owed, and all three digests recomputed against their committed artifacts. Substantive work: verter_compiler assembly gains a typed Fragment / ValidatedFragment / SourceUnit / ProductPlan / compose / publish surface whose composer accepts only validated fragment references, and the live Vue main path was actually cut over to it rather than left dual-path, after a codex ruling refused the implementer's first attempt to defer the cutover as BV1 territory. The former session-private MapComposer, ModuleWriter and FragmentWrite are deleted. Four real production bugs were found and fixed: a render export binding decided by text-scanning generated code, a source-map desync on virtual-file import injection, a CodeTransform pointer-identity bug producing a double-export module, and a separator-less splice that could emit invalid JavaScript. Adversarial review caught and forced removal of a newly-added name-keyed source-tree scanner test, which the landed-scanner bar forbids. Verified independently by the orchestrator: no stubs, no empty test bodies and no always-true assertions in the candidate diff; the three named gate failures are genuinely pre-existing, with external_template_ide_compile_contains_selected_bytes corroborated by B3's own landing record and store_view_build_wall_cost_is_flat_across_host_sizes confirmed as a wall-clock ratio assertion last touched long before this program. Two residuals recorded rather than hidden: the V19 conformance vector is filtered out of one divergence assertion with no forcing function that would fail once the owed spec amendment lands, and a doc comment in assembly/compose.rs still names the three deleted private types. Debt FC-B4-001 and FC-B4-003 remain open with named resolution gates; FC-B4-002 is resolved by this candidate."

   625	notes = "LANDED AND FULLY REVIEWED, BUT NOT ACCEPTED - ITS ENABLING AMENDMENT IS UNRATIFIED. AMD-005 is marked PROPOSED - NOT RATIFIED with no execution authority, and this row's own prior note said the block was not dispatchable before ratification. The program orchestrator unlocked and dispatched it on DAG predecessor satisfaction alone without reading that note; the validator does not gate on amendment ratification, so nothing caught it. The work is real and is left landed rather than reverted, but acceptance is the maintainer's, contingent on ratifying AMD-005 or ruling the block authorised. Identity independently verified: linear fast-forward ff2e0217e to 913d42ce3, zero merges, candidate equals accepted, all three digests recomputed against their committed artifacts. Substance: the Vapor/VDOM conformance backlog is closed against the locked rc.3 oracle, having first been repinned off the stale rc.1 domain that was masking real divergence. Two genuine runtime bugs found and fixed rather than papered over: a silently-dropped slot prop binding, and reactive text updating the wrong DOM node. A ratified BV0-to-BV1 debt row closed for real by un-ignoring its pinned-runtime regression test, and a scope-ordinal bug in the conformance comparator itself fixed - it had been producing false positives, so the oracle was lying in both directions. Orchestrator-verified on the candidate diff: zero stubs, zero newly ignored tests, exactly one un-ignore and it is the genuine debt closure; verter_compiler tests rose 6165 to 6193 with none removed or weakened. All three mandates PASS, but conformance returned BLOCKING on five findings in round one and passed only on a targeted-delta re-review; the implementer fixed two beyond the review's ask, one of which proved to be real data loss.     98	fn assert_exposed_all_materialize(project: &Arc<MetaProject>, fixture_name: &str) {
    99	    let host = project.host();
   100	    let output = host
   101	        .get_component_meta_output("/c.vue")
   102	        .unwrap_or_else(|e| {
   103	            panic!("[{fixture_name}] output materialization must not error, got: {e}")
   104	        })
   105	        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("[{fixture_name}] component must resolve"));
   106	    let (analysis, _resolution, types) = output.into_parts();
   107	    let lanes = types.into_lanes();
   108	    assert_eq!(
   109	        analysis.exposed.len(),
   110	        lanes.exposed.len(),
   111	        "[{fixture_name}] exposed lane must be 1:1 with the analysis"
   112	    );
   113	    for (idx, exposed) in analysis.exposed.iter().enumerate() {
   114	        assert!(
   115	            !matches!(lanes.exposed[idx], TypeExpr::Unknown(_)),
   116	            "[{fixture_name}] exposed[{idx}] (`{}`) must not degrade to Unknown",
   117	            exposed.name
   118	        );
   119	    }
   120	}

   304	/// Finding C — runtime-declared props (`String`/`Number`/`Boolean`
   305	/// constructors) must materialize to their primitive types, not
   306	/// `unknown`. Optionality is checked SEPARATELY: `count`/`enabled` are
   307	/// optional (no `required: true`), so their published type is expected to
   308	/// be `T | undefined`, NOT bare `unknown | undefined`.
   309	#[test]
   310	fn finding_c_runtime_props_materialize_primitive_types() {
   311	    let project = build_project(FIXTURE_RUNTIME_PROPS);
   312	    let host = project.host();
   313	    let output = host
   314	        .get_component_meta_output("/c.vue")
   315	        .expect("output materialization must not error")
   316	        .expect("component must resolve");
   317	    let (analysis, _resolution, types) = output.into_parts();
   318	    let lanes = types.into_lanes();
   319	    assert_eq!(analysis.props.len(), lanes.props.len());
   320	
   321	    for (expected_name, expected_prim) in [
   322	        ("label", verter_type_expr::PrimitiveName::String),
   323	        ("count", verter_type_expr::PrimitiveName::Number),
   324	        ("enabled", verter_type_expr::PrimitiveName::Boolean),
   325	    ] {
   326	        let idx = analysis
   327	            .props
   328	            .iter()
   329	            .position(|p| p.name == expected_name)
   330	            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("prop `{expected_name}` must be declared"));
   331	        let materialized = lanes.props[idx]
   332	            .materialized_type()
   333	            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("prop `{expected_name}` must publish a type"));
   334	        let contains_primitive = |t: &TypeExpr| -> bool {
   335	            match t {
   336	                TypeExpr::Primitive(p) => *p == expected_prim,
   337	                TypeExpr::Union(members) => members
   338	                    .iter()
   339	                    .any(|m| matches!(m, TypeExpr::Primitive(p) if *p == expected_prim)),
   340	                _ => false,
   341	            }
   342	        };
   343	        assert!(
   344	            contains_primitive(materialized),
   345	            "prop `{expected_name}` must materialize primitive {expected_prim:?} \
   346	             (possibly unioned with `undefined`), got: {materialized:?}"
   347	        );
   348	        assert!(
   349	            !matches!(materialized, TypeExpr::Unknown(_)),
   350	            "prop `{expected_name}` must NOT collapse to bare Unknown, got: {materialized:?}"
   351	        );
   352	    }
   353	}

  1403	pub fn build_prepared_type_decl_cache(
  1404	    canonical_id: &str,
  1405	    state: Arc<ShallowFileState>,
  1406	    dep_edges: Arc<FxHashMap<String, String>>,
  1407	    import_canonicalization: Arc<ImportCanonicalization>,
  1408	    interner: &Arc<IdentityInterner>,
  1409	) -> PreparedTypeDeclCache {
  1410	    let mut slots: FxHashMap<verter_type_expr::DeclBindingKey, PreparedTypeDeclSlot> = state
  1411	        .decl_bodies()
  1412	        .header_index()
  1413	        .type_headers
  1414	        .keys()
  1415	        .cloned()
  1416	        .map(|key| (key, Arc::new(PreparedDeclSlot::new())))

  1420	    // fallback, so they need a prepared-decl slot even though they never enter
  1421	    // the file surface. (A name that IS a file symbol already has a slot and
  1422	    // takes precedence.)

  1425	            scope,
  1426	            verter_semantic::analysis::type_eval::AugmentationScopeKind::Global

  1434	        .keys()
  1435	        .map(|key| key.owner)
  1436	        .collect::<FxHashSet<_>>()
  1437	        .into_iter()
  1438	        .map(|owner| (owner, Arc::new(OnceLock::new())))
  1439	        .collect();

  1442	        // Pool the canonical ONCE: every identity minted for this file (and
  1443	        // the sibling value cache) then shares the pooled allocation.
  1444	        canonical_id: interner.intern(canonical_id),
  1445	        state,
  1446	        dep_edges,
  1447	        import_canonicalization,
  1448	        interner: Arc::clone(interner),
  1449	        slots: Arc::new(slots),

     1	//! Shallow declaration-header index — the parse-time symbol inventory.
     2	//!
     3	//! [`build_decl_header_index`] walks a program's top-level statements ONCE
     4	//! and records, per declared symbol: its name, kind, declaration/name
     5	//! spans, type-parameter headers, direct syntactic member headers, and the
     6	//! source-order locators of every contributing top-level statement. It
     7	//! performs NO type lowering — no `lower_ts_type`, no body walks — so an
     8	//! `IndexedReady` publish that builds only this index lowers zero
     9	//! declaration bodies.
    10	//!
    11	//! The index mirrors the NAME REGISTRATION of
    12	//! [`crate::analysis::type_eval_build::build_eval_env`] exactly (file-scope
    13	//! type/value tables, namespace-qualified names, default-export aliasing,
    14	//! augmentation-scope inventories, JSDoc `@typedef` names under TS-decl
    15	//! precedence): a name is in this index if and only if the whole-env walk
    16	//! would register it. The lazy declaration-body service uses the recorded
    17	//! statement locators to lower exactly a demanded symbol's contributing
    18	//! statements through the shared
    19	//! [`crate::analysis::type_eval_build::lower_top_level_statement`] arms.

    46	struct HeaderStatementContext<'a> {

    49	    source: &'a str,

    51	
    52	impl<'a> HeaderStatementContext<'a> {
    53	    fn new(
    54	        statement_index: usize,
    55	        owner: TopLevelStatementOwner,
    56	        vue_ignore_attachment_starts: &'a FxHashSet<u32>,
    57	        source: &'a str,

    59	        Some(Self {

    62	                owner: owner.owner,

    64	            },
    65	            vue_ignore_attachment_starts,
    66	            source,
    67	        })
    68	    }

    70	    fn key(self, name: &str) -> DeclBindingKey {
    71	        DeclBindingKey::new(self.anchor.owner, name)

    73	}

    77	pub struct DeclHeaderContributor {

    82	
    83	/// A `namespace N { … }` block recorded by the shallow walk — one record

    95

   100	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   101	pub struct AugmentationBlockRecord {
