  1727	                execution_status: result.execution_status,
  1728	            });
  1729	        }
  1730	    }
  1731	
  1732	    out
  1733	}
  1734	
  1735	// ── Props ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1736	
  1737	fn extract_props_from_macro(
  1738	    macro_index: usize,
  1739	    prop_fields: &[ResolvedPropInput],
  1740	    default_keys: &std::collections::HashSet<&str>,
  1741	    default_values: &std::collections::HashMap<&str, &str>,
  1742	    evaluated: Option<&crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedComponentTypes>,
  1743	    out: &mut Vec<PropAnalysis>,
  1744	) {
  1745	    if let Some(eval_fields) = expanded_define_props_fields(evaluated, macro_index) {
  1746	        if !eval_fields.is_empty() {
  1747	            for field in eval_fields {
  1748	                let source_row = prop_fields.iter().find(|row| row.field.name == field.name);
  1749	                let source_field = source_row.map(|row| &row.field);
  1750	                let has_default = default_keys.contains(field.name.as_str());
  1751	                let default_value = default_values
  1752	                    .get(field.name.as_str())
  1753	                    .map(|v| v.to_string());
  1754	                let type_expansion = define_props_property_expansion_metadata(
  1755	                    evaluated,
  1756	                    macro_index,
  1757	                    field.name.as_str(),
  1758	                );
  1759	                let publication = publication_from_position(
  1760	                    &field.ty,
  1761	                    type_expansion.as_ref(),
  1762	                    source_row.and_then(|row| row.authored_evidence.clone()),
  1763	                    ResolutionProvenance::SemanticEvaluator,
  1764	                );
  1765	
  1766	                // JSDoc rides the span-borne supply: the source field (analyzer
  1767	                // same-file extraction or the span-sliced macro DTO surface)
  1768	                // carries the description/tags; an expansion-only member with
  1769	                // no source field publishes none.
  1770	                let (description, tags) = source_field
  1771	                    .map(|field| (field.description.clone(), field.tags.clone()))
  1772	                    .unwrap_or_default();
  1773	
  1774	                out.push(PropAnalysis {
  1775	                    name: field.name.clone(),
  1776	                    callable_role: source_row
  1777	                        .map(|row| row.callable_role.clone())
  1778	                        .unwrap_or_default(),
  1779	                    publication,
  1780	                    type_expansion,
  1781	                    required: !field.optional && !has_default,
  1782	                    has_default,
  1783	                    default_value,
  1784	                    description,
  1785	                    tags,
  1786	                    // Structural-fact read from the expanded field.
  1787	                    // `ExpandedField` carries `declared_in_macro_type_arg`
  1788	                    // propagated end-to-end through the resolver stack:
  1789	                    //
  1790	                    // - Parser: `resolve_interface_with_extends`
  1791	                    //   stamps own-body interface members with `true`
  1792	                    //   and heritage-descent members (`extends`,
  1793	                    //   `Omit<...>` source, intersection non-literal
  1794	                    //   arms) with `false`.
  1795	                    // - Semantic propagation:
  1796	                    //   `expand_macro_types_impl_with_expander` and
  1797	                    //   `surface_member_to_expanded_field` thread the
  1798	                    //   fact through `AnalyzedPropField` →
  1799	                    //   `SurfaceMember` → `ExpandedField`.
  1800	                    // - Session prepared-surface walker:
  1801	                    //   `project_prepared_surface_from_expr` threads
  1802	                    //   `from_root_body` through every recursion arm
  1803	                    //   and gates `PreparedSurfaceCacheKey` /
  1804	                    //   `PreparedMemberCacheKey` on it, so two
  1805	                    //   distinct entry contexts publish two distinct
  1806	                    //   cache slots.
  1807	                    //
  1808	                    // For every reference shape — fully-local
  1809	                    // (`defineProps<LocalProps>()`), cross-file simple
  1810	                    // (`import type { Props } from './x';
  1811	                    // defineProps<Props>()`), cross-file heritage
  1812	                    // (`interface Carrier extends Omit<V,'k'> { k: T }`),
  1813	                    // and inline-literal (`defineProps<{ k: T }>()`) —
  1814	                    // `field.declared_in_macro_type_arg` is the
  1815	                    // structurally-correct value.
  1816	                    declared_in_macro_type_arg: field.declared_in_macro_type_arg,
  1817	                });
  1818	            }
  1819	            // NOTE: We intentionally do NOT fall back to prop_fields here.
  1820	            // When the evaluator runs and produces results, it is authoritative —
  1821	            // utility types like Pick/Omit may have intentionally excluded some
  1822	            // prop_fields entries. Adding them back would break filtering.
  1823	            return;
  1824	        }
  1825	    }
  1826	
  1827	    for row in prop_fields {
  1828	        let field = &row.field;
  1829	        let (publication, type_expansion) = resolve_prop_type(row, evaluated);
  1830	        let has_default = default_keys.contains(field.name.as_str());
  1831	        let default_value = default_values
  1832	            .get(field.name.as_str())
  1833	            .map(|v| v.to_string());
  1834	
  1835	        out.push(PropAnalysis {
  1836	            name: field.name.clone(),
  1837	            callable_role: row.callable_role.clone(),
  1838	            publication,
  1839	            type_expansion,
  1840	            required: !field.is_optional && !has_default,
  1841	            has_default,
  1842	            default_value,
  1843	            description: field.description.clone(),
  1844	            tags: field.tags.clone(),
  1845	            declared_in_macro_type_arg: field.declared_in_macro_type_arg,
  1846	        });
  1847	    }
  1848	
  1849	    if let Some(eval_fields) = expanded_define_props_fields(evaluated, macro_index) {
  1850	        let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<String> = prop_fields
  1851	            .iter()
  1852	            .map(|row| row.field.name.clone())
  1853	            .collect();
  1854	        for field in eval_fields {
  1855	            if !seen.insert(field.name.clone()) {
  1856	                continue;
  1857	            }
  1858	
  1859	            let has_default = default_keys.contains(field.name.as_str());
  1860	            let default_value = default_values
  1861	                .get(field.name.as_str())
  1862	                .map(|v| v.to_string());
  1863	            let type_expansion = define_props_property_expansion_metadata(
  1864	                evaluated,
  1865	                macro_index,
  2025	    merged
  2026	}
  2027	
  2028	/// Resolve the prop's `TypeExpr` per the priority chain:
  2029	///
  2030	/// 1. Evaluated `TypeExpr` post-`raise_and_reduce` (when present).
  2031	///    The graph-native projection guarantees no operator-leaf residue
  2032	///    at this layer; the evaluated type IS the authoritative resolved
  2033	///    shape.
  2034	/// 2. Raw annotation (when no evaluated entry exists for this field).
  2035	///    Parsed from the source annotation as the symbolic fallback.
  2036	/// 3. `Unknown { raw: "unknown" }` (when neither is present).
  2037	///
  2038	/// `prefer_symbolic_prop_type_expr` enforces the priority on the
  2039	/// evaluated path; the residual "fall back to raw when evaluated is
  2040	/// incomplete-placeholder" branch in
  2041	/// [`should_prefer_symbolic_prop_type_expr`] is defense-in-depth that
  2042	/// fires only when expansion stops mid-shape (incomplete + budget-
  2043	/// exceeded). When dispatch's `raise_and_reduce` substitution parity
  2044	/// closes the substitution gap documented in
  2045	/// `materialize_component_meta_type_expr_until_stable_full`, the
  2046	/// incomplete-placeholder fallback becomes structurally unreachable
  2047	/// and can be removed.
  2048	fn resolve_prop_type(
  2049	    row: &ResolvedPropInput,
  2050	    evaluated: Option<&crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpandedComponentTypes>,
  2051	) -> (
  2052	    TypePublication,
  2053	    Option<crate::analysis::type_expand::ExpansionMetadata>,
  2054	) {
  2055	    // The row's own session-resolved source is the authority; the flat
  2056	    // evaluated lane contributes ONLY expansion metadata (an INCOMPLETE
  2057	    // expansion still falls back to the author's own annotation position —
  2058	    // the honest symbolic surface, never a torn partial).
  2059	    let metadata = evaluated.and_then(|eval| {
  2060	        eval.props
  2061	            .iter()
  2062	            .find(|f| f.name == row.field.name)
  2063	            .map(field_expansion_metadata)
  2064	    });
  2065	    let publication = TypePublication::new(
  2066	        row.authority.clone(),
  2067	        row.authored_evidence.clone(),
  2068	        &PublicationPolicy::exact_only(),
  2069	    );
  2070	    (publication, metadata)
  2071	}
  2072	
  2073	// ── Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  2074	
  2075	fn event_raw_signature(
  2076	    fallback_raw_type: Option<&str>,
  2077	    source_payload: Option<&str>,
  2078	) -> Option<String> {
  2079	    if let Some(source_payload) = source_payload
  2080	        .map(str::trim)
  2081	        .filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
  2082	    {
  2083	        return Some(source_payload.to_string());
  2084	    }
  2085	    fallback_raw_type
  2086	        .map(str::trim)
  2087	        .filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
  2088	        .map(preserve_or_wrap_event_payload)
  2089	}
  2090	
  2815	
  2816	/// Merge the analyzer's parse-domain prop fields with the host-resolved
  2817	/// rows into ONE per-macro row set, each carrying its member-value SOURCE.
  2818	/// An analyzer-only field's source is its authored payload position (or the
  2819	/// PROVEN unannotated absence for a payload-less runtime field); a
  2820	/// host-resolved row's `type_source` is the normalized-surface authority and
  2821	/// WINS on a same-name merge (the analysis metadata gap-fills through
  2822	/// [`merge_prop_field`]).
  2823	fn merged_prop_fields(
  2824	    mac: &AnalyzedMacro,
  2825	    resolved: Option<&ResolvedMacroInput>,
  2826	) -> Vec<ResolvedPropInput> {
  2827	    let mut rows: Vec<ResolvedPropInput> = mac
  2828	        .prop_fields
  2829	        .iter()
  2830	        .map(|field| {
  2831	            let position = authored_payload_position(field.payload.as_ref());
  2832	            ResolvedPropInput {
  2833	                authority: ResolvedTypeAuthority::from_source_position(
  2834	                    &position,
  2835	                    exactness_from_expansion(None, &position),
  2836	                    ResolutionProvenance::SemanticEvaluator,
  2837	                    std::sync::Arc::from([]),
  2838	                ),
  2839	                authored_evidence: authored_type_evidence(
  2840	                    field.payload.as_ref(),
  2841	                    field.type_annotation.as_deref(),
  2842	                ),
  2843	                callable_role: verter_type_expr::PropCallableRole::default(),
  2844	                field: field.clone(),
  2845	            }
  2846	        })
  2847	        .collect();
  2848	    if let Some(resolved) = resolved {
  2849	        for prop in &resolved.props {
  2850	            if let Some(existing) = rows
  2851	                .iter_mut()
  2852	                .find(|row| row.field.name == prop.field.name)
  2853	            {
  2854	                merge_prop_field(&mut existing.field, &prop.field);
  2855	                // The normalized-surface source is authoritative for the
  2856	                // merged row (it already prefers the PROVEN authored
  2857	                // position when one denotes the resolved member).
  2858	                existing.authority = prop.authority.clone();
  2859	                existing.authored_evidence = prop.authored_evidence.clone();
  2860	                existing.callable_role = prop.callable_role.clone();
  3015	        }
  3016	    }
  3017	    MergedSlotFields {
  3018	        fields,
  3019	        return_publications,
  3020	    }
  3021	}
  3022	
  3023	fn extract_props_from_options(opts: &AnalyzedOptionsApi, out: &mut Vec<PropAnalysis>) {
  3024	    for prop in &opts.props {
  3025	        let raw_type = prop
  3026	            .type_annotation
  3027	            .clone()
  3028	            .or_else(|| prop.type_constructor.clone());
  3029	        // Prefer the authored `PropType<T>` payload position when available;
  3030	        // else fold the primitive runtime constructor to a closed leaf fact
  3031	        // (non-primitive constructors carry display text only — `raw_type`).
  3032	        let type_source = authored_payload_source(prop.payload.as_ref()).or_else(|| {
  3033	            prop.type_constructor.as_ref().and_then(|rt| {
  3034	                use verter_type_expr::facts::{ClosedTypeFact, LeafTypeFact};
  3035	                use verter_type_expr::PrimitiveName;
  3036	                let primitive = match rt.as_str() {
  3037	                    "String" => PrimitiveName::String,
  3038	                    "Number" => PrimitiveName::Number,
  3039	                    "Boolean" => PrimitiveName::Boolean,
  3040	                    _ => return None,
  3041	                };
  3042	                Some(SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(
  3043	                    LeafTypeFact::Primitive(primitive),
  3044	                )))
  3045	            })
  3046	        });
  3047	        out.push(PropAnalysis {
  3048	            name: prop.name.clone(),
  3049	            callable_role: verter_type_expr::PropCallableRole::Other,
  3050	            publication: publication_from_position(
  3051	                &present_or_unannotated(type_source),
  3052	                None,
  3053	                authored_type_evidence(prop.payload.as_ref(), raw_type.as_deref()),
  3054	                ResolutionProvenance::SemanticEvaluator,
  3055	            ),
  3056	            type_expansion: None,
  3057	            // Options API path: no authored companion for the raw display
  3058	            // text (the typed source is above).
  3059	            required: prop.is_required,
  3060	            has_default: prop.has_default,
  3061	            default_value: prop.default_value.clone(),
  3062	            description: prop.description.clone(),
  3063	            tags: prop.tags.clone(),
  3064	            // Options API props are explicit author declarations in the
  3065	            // `props: { ... }` object on the component's options block —
  2975	struct RuntimePropExtraction {
  2976	    fields: Vec<AnalyzedPropField>,
  2977	    default_keys: Vec<String>,
  2978	    default_values: Vec<AnalyzedDefaultValue>,
  2979	}
  2980	
  2981	/// Map a runtime constructor name to its TypeScript type string.
  2982	fn constructor_to_ts_type(name: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
  2983	    match name {
  2984	        "String" => Some("string"),
  2985	        "Number" => Some("number"),
  2986	        "Boolean" => Some("boolean"),
  2987	        "Array" => Some("Array<any>"),
  2988	        "Object" => Some("object"),
  2989	        "Function" => Some("Function"),
  2990	        "Symbol" => Some("symbol"),
  2991	        "Date" => Some("Date"),
  2992	        "RegExp" => Some("RegExp"),
  2993	        "Promise" => Some("Promise<any>"),
  2994	        _ => None,
  2995	    }
  2996	}
  2997	
  2998	/// Whether a runtime prop's `as` assertion carries an authored payload TYPE
  2999	/// position. Presence-only — the payload position is stamped at the macro's
  3000	/// final index; the typed body is demanded through the shared dispatch on read.
  3001	///
  3002	/// Rules:
  3003	/// - `X as PropType<T>` → the `T` argument position
  3004	/// - `X as () => T` / `X as new () => T` → the return-type position
  3005	/// - Other assertions → no authored payload (caller falls back to
  3006	///   `constructor_to_ts_type`)
  3007	fn has_authored_prop_type_assertion(ts_as: &TSAsExpression<'_>) -> bool {
  3008	    match &ts_as.type_annotation {
  3009	        TSType::TSTypeReference(type_ref) => {
  3010	            if let TSTypeName::IdentifierReference(id) = &type_ref.type_name {
  3011	                id.name == "PropType"
  3012	                    && type_ref
  3013	                        .type_arguments
  3014	                        .as_ref()
  3015	                        .is_some_and(|args| !args.params.is_empty())
  3016	            } else {
  3017	                false
  3018	            }
  3019	        }
  3020	        TSType::TSFunctionType(_) | TSType::TSConstructorType(_) => true,
  3021	        _ => false,
  3022	    }
  3023	}
  3024	
  3025	/// Extract prop fields from a runtime argument (object or array).
  3026	///
  3027	/// For object form, detects both shorthand (`name: String`) and expanded
  3028	/// (`name: { type: String, default: 'Hello' }`) property definitions.
  3029	fn extract_prop_fields_from_runtime(
  3030	    expr: &Expression<'_>,
  3031	    source: &str,
  3032	    comments: &[Comment],
  3033	) -> RuntimePropExtraction {
  3034	    match expr {
  3035	        Expression::ObjectExpression(obj) => {
  3036	            let mut fields = Vec::new();
  3037	            let mut default_keys = Vec::new();
  3038	            let mut default_values = Vec::new();
  3039	
  3040	            for prop in &obj.properties {
  3041	                let ObjectPropertyKind::ObjectProperty(p) = prop else {
  3042	                    continue;
  3043	                };
  3044	                let key_name = match &p.key {
  3045	                    PropertyKey::StaticIdentifier(id) => id.name.to_string(),
  3046	                    PropertyKey::StringLiteral(lit) => lit.value.to_string(),
  3047	                    _ => continue,
  3048	                };
  3049	
  3050	                let mut type_annotation: Option<String> = None;
  3051	                // Whether an authored `PropType<T>`-style assertion exists (the
  3052	                // payload position is stamped at the macro's final index).
  3053	                let mut has_authored_prop_type = false;
  3054	                // Vue semantics: props are optional by default unless `required: true` is set.
  3055	                let mut is_optional = true;
  3056	
  3057	                // Check if value is a constructor (shorthand: `name: String`)
  3058	                if let Expression::Identifier(id) = &p.value {
  3059	                    if let Some(ts_text) = constructor_to_ts_type(&id.name) {
  3060	                        type_annotation = Some(ts_text.to_string());
  3061	                    }
  3062	                }
  3063	
  3064	                // Check if value is an expanded object: `name: { type: String, default: 'Hello' }`
  3065	                if let Expression::ObjectExpression(val_obj) = &p.value {
  3066	                    for sub_prop in &val_obj.properties {
  3067	                        let ObjectPropertyKind::ObjectProperty(sp) = sub_prop else {
  3068	                            continue;
  3069	                        };
  3070	                        let sub_key = match &sp.key {
  3071	                            PropertyKey::StaticIdentifier(id) => id.name.as_str(),
  3072	                            _ => continue,
  3073	                        };
  3074	                        match sub_key {
  3075	                            "type" => {
  3076	                                // Try to extract an explicit type assertion first (`X as PropType<T>`,
  3077	                                // `X as () => T`, `X as new () => T`), then fall back to mapping the
  3078	                                // base constructor identifier via `constructor_to_ts_type`.
  3079	                                if let Expression::TSAsExpression(ts_as) = &sp.value {
  3080	                                    if has_authored_prop_type_assertion(ts_as) {
  3081	                                        // Display: slice the source span of the inner type-arg / return-type
  3082	                                        // so the wire payload still carries human-readable text.
  3083	                                        let display_span = match &ts_as.type_annotation {
  3084	                                            TSType::TSTypeReference(tr) => tr
  3085	                                                .type_arguments
  3086	                                                .as_ref()
  3087	                                                .and_then(|args| args.params.first())
  3088	                                                .map(|first| first.span()),
  3089	                                            TSType::TSFunctionType(ft) => {
  3090	                                                Some(ft.return_type.type_annotation.span())
  3091	                                            }
  3092	                                            TSType::TSConstructorType(ct) => {
  3093	                                                Some(ct.return_type.type_annotation.span())
  3094	                                            }
  3095	                                            _ => None,
  3096	                                        };
  3097	                                        type_annotation = display_span.and_then(|sp_| {
  3098	                                            let s = sp_.start as usize;
  3099	                                            let e = sp_.end as usize;
  3100	                                            (e <= source.len())
  3101	                                                .then(|| source[s..e].trim().to_string())
  3102	                                                .filter(|t| !t.is_empty())
  3103	                                        });
  3104	                                        has_authored_prop_type = true;
  3105	                                    } else if let Expression::Identifier(id) = &ts_as.expression {
  3106	                                        if let Some(ts_text) = constructor_to_ts_type(&id.name) {
  3107	                                            type_annotation = Some(ts_text.to_string());
  3108	                                        }
  3109	                                    }
  3110	                                } else if let Expression::Identifier(id) = &sp.value {
  3111	                                    if let Some(ts_text) = constructor_to_ts_type(&id.name) {
  3112	                                        type_annotation = Some(ts_text.to_string());
  3113	                                    }
  3114	                                }
  3115	                            }
  3116	                            "required" => {
  3117	                                // `required: true` makes the prop required (not optional).
  3118	                                if let Expression::BooleanLiteral(b) = &sp.value {
  3119	                                    is_optional = !b.value;
  3120	                                }
  3121	                            }
  3122	                            "default" => {
  3123	                                let val_text = default_value_source_text(&sp.value, source)
  3124	                                    .unwrap_or_default();
  3125	                                default_keys.push(key_name.clone());
  3126	                                default_values.push(AnalyzedDefaultValue {
  3127	                                    key: key_name.clone(),
  3128	                                    value: val_text,
  3129	                                    span: sp.value.span().into(),
  3130	                                });
  3131	                            }
  3132	                            _ => {}
  3133	                        }
  3134	                    }
  3135	                }
  3136	
  3137	                let (description, tags) = extract_jsdoc_for(comments, p.key.span().start, source);
  3138	
  3139	                let type_expr_scope =
  3140	                    has_authored_prop_type.then(|| verter_type_expr::TypeExprScope::new(""));
  3141	                fields.push(AnalyzedPropField {
  3142	                    name: key_name,
  3143	                    is_optional,
  3144	                    span: p.key.span().into(),
  3145	                    type_annotation,
  3146	                    description,
  3147	                    tags,
  3148	                    resolution_source: TypeResolutionSource::Rust,
  3149	                    resolution_error: None,
  3150	                    payload: None,
  3151	                    type_expr_scope,
  3152	                    // Runtime object form — the author wrote this prop name
  3153	                    // directly as a key in `defineProps({ ... })`.
  3154	                    declared_in_macro_type_arg: true,
  3155	                });
  3156	            }
  3157	
  3158	            RuntimePropExtraction {
  3159	                fields,
  3160	                default_keys,
   150	
   151	        // props: { foo: String, bar: { type: Number, required: true } }
   152	        Expression::ObjectExpression(obj) => obj
   153	            .properties
   154	            .iter()
   155	            .filter_map(|prop| {
   156	                let ObjectPropertyKind::ObjectProperty(p) = prop else {
   157	                    return None;
   158	                };
   159	                let name = static_key_name(&p.key)?;
   160	                let span = key_span(&p.key);
   161	                let (description, tags) = extract_jsdoc_for(comments, p.key.span().start, source);
   162	
   163	                match &p.value {
   164	                    // Shorthand: `foo: String`
   165	                    Expression::Identifier(id) => Some(AnalyzedOptionsProp {
   166	                        name,
   167	                        span,
   168	                        type_constructor: Some(id.name.to_string()),
   169	                        is_required: false,
   170	                        has_default: false,
   171	                        default_value: None,

  4419	/// Render a syntactic call shape as a declaration-legal function type.
  4420	///
  4421	/// The parameters are the AUTHORED ones — their names (so a consumer's
  4422	/// signature help reads like the source) and their arity — each typed `any`,

  4427	/// member can be CALLED at all.

  4430	    // required parameter after an optional one (TS1016). JavaScript has no such
  4431	    // rule — `function focus(target = 0, mode) {}` is fine, and a caller reaches
  4432	    // `mode` by passing `undefined` for `target` — so the authored optionality
  4433	    // is a FACT that cannot always be expressed. Where it cannot, the parameter
  4434	    // renders REQUIRED: a caller must pass something positionally anyway, and
  4435	    // the alternative is a declaration that does not compile at all.

  4437	    // So find where the trailing all-optional run begins and mark only from
  4438	    // there. `(a = 1, b)` renders `(a: any, b: any)`; `(a, b = 1)` renders

  4440	    // parameter never blocks the run — `(a?: any, ...rest: any[])` is legal.

  4442	        .params

  4444	        .rposition(|param| !param.optional)
  4445	        .map_or(0, |last_required| last_required + 1);

  4450	            rendered.push_str(", ");
  4451	        }

    71	
    72	## Finding B — root cause
    73	
    74	### The literal error text vs. what actually happens
    75	
    76	`"component-meta output materialization failed at exposed[].type index <N>: the source has no
    77	live graph representation under the request view"` is produced by exactly one place:
    78	`ComponentMetaOutputError`'s `Display` impl for the `UnraisableSource` variant
    79	(`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/output.rs:562-564`). That variant is only reached when
    80	a lane's `SourcePosition` is `Present(source)` **and** the shared raise
    81	(`ProjectSemanticDispatch::raise_semantic_type_source_to_hot_strict`,
    82	`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/semantic_source.rs:428`) returns `Ok(None)`
    83	for a disposition that isn't a legitimate carrier
    84	(`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink.rs:1216-1273`).
    85	
    86	**In every fixture I constructed, the exposed member's `SourcePosition` is never `Present` in
    87	the first place — it is `Absent(SchemaAbsence::Unannotated)`.** Per
    88	`materialize_output_lane_slot` (`crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink/envelope.rs:144-171`),
    89	an `Absent` position is a documented, intentional success path: it renders
    90	`missing_source_output_type_expr()` = `TypeExpr::Unknown(UnknownValue::missing_output())`
    91	**with no error at all** (`Ok(missing_source_output_type_expr())`, not
    92	`Err(ComponentMetaOutputFailure::…)`). That is exactly the value my repro observes:
    93	`Unknown(UnknownValue { raw: "", provenance: MissingOutput })`, and `get_component_meta_output`
    94	returns `Ok(Some(..))`, not `Err(..)`.
    95	
    96	So the symptom I can reproduce in-repo is **upstream** of the raise/materialize step the task
    97	brief's hypothesis targeted: the exposed binding never gets a `Present` source at all, so the
    98	strict raise path is never entered and never has a chance to fail loudly.
    99	
   100	### The actual mechanism
   101	
   102	`ExposedAnalysis::type_source` (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs:453-462`)
   103	is set by `resolve_exposed_type` (same file, line 2794):
   104	
   105	```rust
   106	fn resolve_exposed_type(name, bindings, evaluated) -> Option<SemanticTypeSource> {
   107	    if let Some(eval) = evaluated {
   108	        if let Some(f) = eval.bindings.iter().find(|f| f.name == name) {
   109	            return match f.authority.outcome() {
   110	                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Present { source, .. } => Some(source.as_ref().clone()),
   111	                ResolvedTypeOutcome::Absent { .. } | ResolvedTypeOutcome::Failed { .. } => None,
   112	            };
   113	        }
   114	    }
   115	    None   // <-- the name was never even offered
   116	}
   117	```
   118	
   119	For an object-literal `defineExpose({ a, b })` (the common, documented Vue form — as opposed to
   120	the type-argument `defineExpose<T>()` form, which is a separate, working code path through
   121	`meta_resolve/projectors/exposed.rs`), the ONLY way an exposed name reaches
   122	`eval.bindings` is via the general macro-argument-type expansion's **binding-entry admission
   123	gate**:
   124	
   125	`crates/verter_session/src/host_manage/eval_env.rs::component_meta_binding_type_entries`
   126	(lines ~907-956):
   127	
   128	```rust
   129	admitted
   130	    .iter()
   131	    .filter(|binding| {
   132	        ctx.prepared_value_decl(canonical, binding.owner, binding.name.as_ref())
   133	            .is_some_and(|decl| {
   134	                !matches!(
   135	                    decl.type_annotation.classification,
   136	                    verter_type_expr::facts::ValueAnnotationClass::Absent
   137	                )
   138	            })
   139	    })
   140	    .map(|binding| BindingExpansionEntry { name: …, owner: … })
   141	    .collect()
   142	```
   143	
   144	This is a **deliberate, documented gate** ("the `defineExpose` binding-entry NAMES the macro
   145	expander emits … the same has-annotation gate the retired typed-entry list applied") — but it
   146	checks **only** `PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation.classification`. It silently drops any
   147	binding whose type-bearing evidence lives somewhere else on `PreparedValueDecl`:
   148	
   149	- `PreparedValueDecl.signatures: Vec<FunctionSignature>` — a plain `function` **declaration**'s
   150	  type. Confirmed: `function focus(): void {}` still fails even with an explicit return type,
   151	  because a function declaration's type is never carried on `.type_annotation` at all — it's
   152	  structurally a `signatures`-only decl. The gate has no branch for this.
   153	- Whatever carries the type for a `const x = ref(0)` / `const x: Ref<number> = ref(0)`
   154	  initializer. I traced the general variable-declarator lowering
   155	  (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_eval_build.rs::lower_variable_declarator_parts`,
   156	  ~lines 3260-3394) and its `value_type_derives_from_a_call` branch (line 5997) — by that
   157	  reading, `expression_source_offset` should be set for a call-expression initializer, and an
   158	  *explicit* `Ref<number>` annotation should short-circuit straight to
   159	  `ValueAnnotationClass::Direct` via `value_type_annotation_fact`
   160	  (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/fact_projection.rs:78-153`) regardless of the call.
   161	  That did **not** match the observed behavior (still `Absent` even with the explicit
   162	  annotation) — **I could not fully close this gap within budget.** Either
   163	  `lower_variable_declarator_parts` is not actually the code path invoked for `<script setup>`
   164	  top-level bindings in a `.vue` carrier (there may be a separate SFC/framework-specific binding
   165	  lowering that doesn't thread the same annotation/call logic), or `prepared_value_decl`'s
   166	  lookup (`visible_value_binding` / owner resolution) fails to find `count`/`doubled` at all for
   167	  a reason unrelated to annotation classification. Either way, the **admission gate is the
   168	  point where the binding is lost**, confirmed by direct instrumentation (see next section) —
   169	  what I couldn't pin down is which specific upstream producer fails to feed it.
   170	
   171	### Direct evidence (from the diagnostic traces run during this investigation, now folded into
   172	the isolation tests above)
   173	
   174	| Fixture | `exposed[].type_source` |
   175	|---|---|
   176	| `const x: number = 5` | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   177	| `const b: Box<number> = { value: 1 }` (local generic, no call) | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   178	| `const focus: () => void = () => {}` (arrow expr, no call) | `Present(Authored(DeclBody(...)))` |
   179	| `const count = ref(0)` (untyped, call init) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   180	| `const count: Ref<number> = ref(0)` (typed, call init) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   181	| `function focus(): void {}` (declaration) | `Absent(Unannotated)` |
   182	
   183	The pattern is exact and reproducible: **any exposed binding that is either (a) a plain
   184	function declaration, or (b) a `const` whose initializer is a call expression — regardless of
   185	whether it carries an explicit type annotation — is silently dropped before it ever reaches a
   186	`Present` source position.** This covers exactly the two shapes a real-world Options-free Vue 3
   187	component's `defineExpose` almost always uses: exposed methods, and exposed `ref()`/`computed()`
   188	state. That matches the task's four failing real fixtures (methods, refs/computed, full-API,
   189	runtime-props) far better than a raise-time failure would.
   190	
   191	### Contract violated / owner
   192	
   193	This violates the Component-Meta Shallow-By-Default / general "no silent Unknown for a
   194	present-in-source binding" expectation — a `defineExpose`d name that is lexically visible and
   195	has a perfectly good type (inferable from `ref`'s signature, or the function's own signature) is
   196	being treated identically to "the author wrote no type at all." The owning layer is
   197	`verter_session`'s component-meta binding-type-entry admission gate
   198	(`host_manage/eval_env.rs::component_meta_binding_type_entries`) plus, contingent on the
   199	open trace gap above, possibly the variable-declarator/binding lowering that feeds
   200	`PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation` for `<script setup>` scopes. This is **squarely inside
   201	`verter_session`'s existing analysis/expansion pipeline** — a narrow, local fix (make the gate
   202	also admit when `!decl.signatures.is_empty()`, and close the call-expression-initializer gap in
   203	whichever producer is actually in play for SFC bindings). **It does not require C1's
   204	request-view/lifecycle rework** — nothing here is about view identity, request-scoping, or
   205	resolver-caching; it's a pre-existing admission filter dropping legitimate candidates before any
   206	raise/dispatch step is reached.
   207	
   208	### What I could not determine for Finding B

   228	
   229	## Finding C — root cause
   230	
   231	### Reproduction detail
   232	
   233	`defineProps({ label: String, count: Number, enabled: Boolean })` — `label` materializes to
   234	`Unknown(UnknownValue{raw:"", provenance: MissingOutput})`. Same failure class as Finding B:
   235	**`Absent` schema position, silently rendered**, not a raise-time error.
   236	
   237	### Mechanism
   238	
   239	There are two structurally parallel prop-extraction paths in
   240	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs`:
   241	
   242	1. **Options API** (`export default { props: {...} } `) — `extract_props_from_options`
   243	   (line 3023). This path **does** special-case runtime constructors: it reads
   244	   `prop.type_constructor: Option<String>` (populated at parse time in
   245	   `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/options.rs:168-233` from the identifier name `String`/
   246	   `Number`/`Boolean`) and maps it into a real, closed semantic fact:
   247	   ```rust
   248	   let primitive = match rt.as_str() {
   249	       "String" => PrimitiveName::String,
   250	       "Number" => PrimitiveName::Number,
   251	       "Boolean" => PrimitiveName::Boolean,
   252	       _ => return None,
   253	   };
   254	   Some(SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(LeafTypeFact::Primitive(primitive))))
   255	   ```
   256	
   257	2. **Composition API macro** (`defineProps({...})` inside `<script setup>`) — the code path my
   258	   repro exercises — `extract_props_from_macro` (line 1737), non-type-based fallback
   259	   (`mac.is_type_based == false`), which builds each `PropAnalysis.publication` from
   260	   `resolve_prop_type(row, evaluated)` off `row.field`'s **authored payload position**
   261	   (`field.payload: Option<MacroPayloadLocator>`).
   262	
   263	The runtime-constructor recognizer for the macro path,
   264	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs::constructor_to_ts_type` (line 2982), **only
   265	produces a display-only text string** (`AnalyzedPropField.type_annotation: Option<String>` —
   266	explicitly documented elsewhere in this codebase as a display-only passthrough that must never
   267	feed semantic decisions). For the shorthand form (`label: String`) and the bare `type: String`
   268	form, `constructor_to_ts_type`'s result is written **only** to `type_annotation` (display text)
   269	— `field.payload` (the thing `authored_payload_position`/`resolve_prop_type` actually reads to
   270	build a `SemanticTypeSource`) is left `None` unless the author wrote an explicit `X as
   271	PropType<T>` assertion (`has_authored_prop_type_assertion`,
   272	`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs:2998-3023`, gated by
   273	`type_expr_scope = has_authored_prop_type.then(...)` at line 3139-3140).
   274	
   275	So: for the ordinary, most-common `defineProps({ label: String })` runtime-declaration form,
   276	**no typed semantic source is ever constructed at all** — only a throwaway display string. The
   277	field's `SourcePosition` therefore resolves as genuinely `Absent`, and the output sink correctly
   278	(per its own contract) renders that as `Unknown`.
   279	
   280	### Why optionality survives but the type doesn't
   281	
   282	`required`/`has_default` in `extract_props_from_macro`'s fallback loop
   283	(`component_meta.rs:1827-1846`) is computed independently, from `field.is_optional` (a bool set
   284	directly from whether `required: true` was seen in `macros.rs::extract_prop_fields_from_runtime`,
   285	line 3055/3116-3120) and `default_keys`/`default_values` — none of which route through
   286	`field.payload`/`resolve_prop_type` at all. That's a disjoint, working computation, which is
   287	exactly why the task's observed behavior is "optionality survives, primitive type is lost."
   288	
   289	### Contract violated / owner
   290	
   291	This is a **parity gap between the Options-API and Composition-API (macro) prop-extraction
   292	paths** inside `verter_semantic::analysis` — the Options API already does the correct thing
   293	(map a recognized runtime constructor identifier to a closed primitive semantic fact at the
   294	analyzer/extraction layer, not at the output seam); the macro path never got (or lost) the
   295	equivalent. This is **not** a case of "no source exists for this position" — the source (the
   296	literal identifier `String`) is right there in the AST; the analyzer captures it as display text
   297	and then discards the semantic identity. The correct fix location is the same layer the Options
   298	API path already uses correctly: `crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs`'s
   299	`extract_prop_fields_from_runtime` (or a shared helper it and `analysis/options.rs` both call)
   300	should mint a `SemanticTypeSource::Closed(ClosedTypeFact::Leaf(LeafTypeFact::Primitive(...)))` (or
   301	populate an equivalent typed locator on `AnalyzedPropField`) for a recognized runtime
   302	constructor, mirroring what `extract_props_from_options` already does — **not** a hard-coded
   303	string-to-primitive mapping at the final output seam (which the task's hard prohibitions
   304	correctly rule out).
   305	
   306	This is **fixable under the current architecture** — it's a straightforward analyzer-layer
   307	parity fix between two already-existing, structurally-similar extraction functions in the same
   308	file family. No request-view/lifecycle rework is implicated.
   309	
   310	### What I could not determine for Finding C
   311	
   312	- I did not check whether the same gap applies to the `{ type: String, default: '...' }`
   313	  expanded object form specifically (vs. the shorthand `label: String` form) — the code reads as
   314	  identically affected (both write only to `type_annotation` via the same `constructor_to_ts_type`
   315	  call, `macros.rs:3110-3114`), but I did not add a fixture for it.
   316	- I did not check whether arrays of constructors (`label: [String, Number]`) or `PropType<T>`
   317	  the CORRECT way already work end-to-end (they should, per the `has_authored_prop_type`
   318	  branch, which does populate `type_expr_scope`/a payload position) — this is consistent with
   319	  the code but I did not add a positive-control fixture proving it in-repo.
   320	- I did not check whether this same defect surfaces identically for `defineModel` or Options-API
   321	  `props: [...]` (array shorthand) — out of scope for the reported fixtures but worth a sweep
   322	  before landing a fix.
   323	
   324	---
   325

    92	        // macro of this kind from the owner's authoritative shallow snapshot

   100	                        macro_index: None,
   101	                        macro_kind: Self::macro_kind_for(kind),

   109	    fn normalize(
   110	        &self,
   111	        _ctx: &FrameworkAdapterCtx<'_>,
   112	        resolved: ResolvedSurfaces,
   113	    ) -> NormalizedSurfaces {
   114	        let mut surfaces = Vec::new();
   115	        for item in resolved.items {
   116	            // Vue plans only macro-payload demands, and only a macro-payload
   117	            // resolution carries a per-kind DTO bundle; any other resolved-demand
   118	            // arm in the closed taxonomy is not a Vue wire surface and is skipped.
   119	            let ResolvedDemand::MacroPayload(payload) = item.result else {
   120	                continue;
   180	        };
   181	        // Build a minimal ctx purely to satisfy the signature; planning ignores
   182	        // it.
   183	        let host = crate::VerterHost::new_standalone(crate::HostConfig::default());
   184	        let registry = crate::framework::FrameworkAdapterRegistry::built_in();
   185	        let registration = registry
   186	            .get(&crate::framework::FrameworkAdapterId::vue())
   187	            .expect("vue registered");
   188	        let ctx = FrameworkAdapterCtx::new(registration, &host);
   189	        let plan = adapter.plan_surfaces(
   190	            &ctx,
   191	            &selector,
   192	            crate::framework::descriptor::ALL_FRAMEWORK_SURFACE_KINDS,
   193	        );
   194	        for item in &plan.items {
   195	            if let PlannedDemand::MacroPayload { selector, .. } = &item.demand {
   196	                assert_eq!(
   197	                    selector.macro_index, None,
   198	                    "planning must not fabricate a macro index for {:?}",
   199	                    selector.macro_kind
   200	                );
   201	            }
   202	        }
   203	        // Every macro surface kind is planned (six macro-payload demands).
   204	        let macro_payloads = plan
   205	            .items
   206	            .iter()
   207	            .filter(|i| matches!(i.demand, PlannedDemand::MacroPayload { .. }))
   208	            .count();
   209	        assert_eq!(macro_payloads, 6, "all six macro surfaces are planned");
   210	    }

## Decision

Create **CM1 under Path A**. Neither known regression requires C1. Treat the benchmark’s `UnraisableSource` as a separate live defect in the same output lane, not as an invocation-route presentation of `Unknown(MissingOutput)`.

### 1. Discrepancy ruling

The two symptoms are mutually exclusive control-flow states:

- `SourcePosition::Absent` returns successful `Unknown(MissingOutput)` at [envelope.rs:154](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink/envelope.rs:154).
- `UnraisableSource` can arise only after a `Present(source)` enters strict raising and yields no graph handle at [output_sink.rs:1221](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink.rs:1221) and [output_sink.rs:1273](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink.rs:1273).
- The NAPI scalar and batch routes use the same materialized envelope; batch explicitly preserves scalar failure semantics at [meta.rs:280](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_napi/src/meta.rs:280) and [meta.rs:303](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_napi/src/meta.rs:303). The host also preserves the typed error at [component_meta_host.rs:73](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/component_meta_host.rs:73).

Therefore, this is **not one defect surfacing differently by invocation route**. The reproduced defect incorrectly produces `Absent`; the benchmark reached `Present` with an invalid/unavailable graph representation. Given the ratified observation, the latter remains a distinct release blocker until the exact benchmark fixture—or a faithful minimized extraction—proves otherwise.

CM1 must repair both states: restore missing producers for B/C and trace the benchmark’s `Present` locator to its owning producer. It must not demote the latter to `Absent` or `unknown`.

### 2. Repair rulings

**Finding B**

The admission predicate is architecturally wrong. It admits only non-`Absent` annotations at [eval_env.rs:938](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/host_manage/eval_env.rs:938), although `PreparedValueDecl` separately owns signatures and object shapes at [prepared.rs:390](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_solver/prepared.rs:390) and [prepared.rs:395](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_solver/prepared.rs:395). Function declarations intentionally lower with no value annotation and a signature at [type_eval_build.rs:2823](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_eval_build.rs:2823).

The correct repair is to admit every structurally demanded, lexically visible local value binding and let the single prepared-value resolver choose among annotation/expression source, object shape, signatures, enum or class facts. That resolver already handles expression sources at [build.rs:741](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/build.rs:741) and signatures at [build.rs:840](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/build.rs:840). A `!signatures.is_empty()` patch alone is insufficient.

For the call-initializer residual, both typed and untyped calls should already be `Direct`: explicit annotations become `Direct` at [fact_projection.rs:140](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/fact_projection.rs:140), while an untyped call’s expression source becomes `Direct` at [fact_projection.rs:101](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/fact_projection.rs:101). CM1 must trace the owner/lookup/preparation handoff and correct the earliest divergence; no call-expression allowlist is acceptable.

Finally, `resolve_exposed_type` must stop collapsing `Failed` and `Absent` together at [component_meta.rs:2801](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs:2801). Preserve `SourcePosition`/authority through publication so a demanded binding that cannot be prepared fails strictly.

**Finding C**

The Options-API path’s **semantic result is the model**: recognized primitive constructors become producer-owned closed facts at [component_meta.rs:3029](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs:3029). Closed facts are intentionally materialized without graph raising at [output_sink.rs:1206](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink.rs:1206).

The macro path instead stores constructor meaning only in display text at [macros.rs:3057](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/macros.rs:3057), while `AnalyzedPropField.type_annotation` is explicitly display-only at [types.rs:1111](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/types.rs:1111).

Repair this at structural AST analysis: introduce one typed runtime-constructor fact/enum shared by Options and macro extraction, and lower exact `String`/`Number`/`Boolean` identities to `ClosedTypeFact::Primitive`. Do not copy the Options path’s current late string switch literally, parse display text, or map names at the output seam. Expanded `{ type: String }`, required/default forms and negative custom/array/`PropType<T>` controls belong in CM1’s matrix.

### 3. Path and placement

Both repairs—and the separate benchmark locator failure—are **Path A**. They concern candidate admission, semantic fact production and locator validity. C1 explicitly preserves current answers and does not own component-meta publication policy at [C1.md:50](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:50) and [C1.md:56](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:56). The error wording mentions a request view; it does not establish that immutable-observation architecture is required.

Confirm:

```text
{BV1, BS1} ──> CM1 ──> C1
{BV1, BS1} ──> BV2 ──> B5
```

CM1 and BV2 are independent siblings; add no edge between them. C2 already reconverges B5 and C1 at [program-dag.toml:165](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program-dag.toml:165). Beta.4 requires both branches accepted. E1 is a later graph-protocol consumer at [program-dag.toml:232](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program-dag.toml:232), not the owner of these regressions.

### 4. Cross-product ruling

- All native, compat, resolved and batch component-meta surfaces are affected because they share the same native output pipeline. **Owner: CM1.**
- PublicApi/TSC is not affected by B: runtime expose emits `typeof` at [script.rs:5981](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_compiler/src/tsc/script.rs:5981). TSX preserves `defineExpose` at [integration_tests.rs:409](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_compiler/src/ide/script/tests/integration_tests.rs:409).
- C’s runtime constructors are already correct in TSC/Public output at [tests.rs:1727](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_compiler/src/tsc/tests.rs:1727).
- Declaration output has a separate B fidelity gap: call-initialized values become `unknown`, while functions become `(...): any`, by explicit policy at [script.rs:6003](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_compiler/src/tsc/script.rs:6003) and [script.rs:6015](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_compiler/src/tsc/script.rs:6015). **Owner: BV2**, because Vue declarations/tooling and source-local macros are BV-owned at [BV1.md:21](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/BV1.md:21).
- The framework-surface semantic API also returns runtime-object macros as memberless because it rejects non-type-based macros at [vue_exec/mod.rs:533](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/framework_surface/vue_exec/mod.rs:533). This affects both runtime `defineExpose` and runtime `defineProps` membership. **Owner: BV2**, not C3; C3 explicitly excludes runtime object syntax at [C3.md:33](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C3.md:33). The general semantic dispatcher itself is not missing the necessary value capabilities.

No ruling changes an accepted ADR or the final program target. The placement ruling changes the DAG by adding CM1 and making C1 depend on it. The discrepancy changes beta.4 release eligibility: the hard-error fixture is an additional CM1 acceptance condition. Blast-radius findings add acceptance coverage to the already-approved BV2 branch, not another edge.

DISCREPANCY: Distinct defects—reproduced `Absent→Unknown` and benchmark `Present→UnraisableSource`; both remain beta.4 blockers.

REPAIR B: Structurally admit demanded visible value bindings, fix the call-binding owner/preparation handoff, and preserve `Failed` through publication.

REPAIR C: Make the Options path’s closed primitive semantics the shared analyzer model; never derive semantics from display text or at the output seam.

PLACEMENT: `{BV1, BS1}→CM1→C1` alongside independent `{BV1, BS1}→BV2→B5`; both gate beta.4, with no E1 deferral.

BLAST-RADIUS: Component-meta variants belong to CM1; declaration and runtime framework-surface gaps belong to BV2; PublicApi/TSC/TSX are not degraded by these two component-meta defects.
